title: Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit ‘Congo Boy’ (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:02am PT Outsider Pictures Takes U.S. on Rafiki Fariala’s Award-Winning Cannes Hit ‘Congo Boy’ (EXCLUSIVE) The film, inspired by Fariala's own experience as a young refugee, unspools at Toronto and is set for a 2027 U.S. release By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Mart Spotlights Ancient Rome, 19th Century Paris, Retired Spooks, Luchadores, Diplomatic Intrigue and Gaza 1 day ago Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Boards Palestinian Art and Resistance Documentary ‘Freedom Theatre’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Patricio Valladares Descends Into Hell With Horror Adaptation of Dante’s ‘Inferno’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago See All 'Congo Boy' Courtesy of The Party Film Sales/Outsider Pictures Santa Monica-based Outsider Pictures has picked up Rafiki Fariala ’s award-winning Cannes title “ Congo Boy ” for the U.S. ahead of its North American premiere at Toronto. Courtesy of Makongo Films/Unité/Kiripifilms/Karta Film/Canal+ The film bowed in Cannes’ Un Certain Regard, where it won Bradley Fiomona the best actor prize for his role as 17-year-old Robert, whose family was forced to flee the Democratic Republic of Congo for the neighboring Central African Republic. With his parents are imprisoned, Robert does what he can to care for his four younger siblings while attending high school, hoping to get into medical school and finding musical success despite all the odds stacked against him. Related Stories Netflix Hires Warner Bros. Exec Katie Martin Kelley as Communications VP Rafael Nadal Docuseries ‘Rafa’: How a Local Setting, Language and Intimate Lensing Set the Primetime Emmy Contender Apart Variety’s Murtada Elfadl praised the film as a “stirring musical drama” that “beats with the rhythms of resilience.” Popular on Variety “Congo Boy” is set to play a number of fall festivals in the U.S. ahead of a planned release in the spring of 2027. “I will be releasing the film in as many cities as I can since the film deals with the hardships of life but also our dreams, and right now everyone can relate to that and the film is ultimately an upbeat audience friendly film,” Outsider Pictures founder and CEO Paul Hudson told Variety . The film’s story very much parallels that of Fariala’s life. A Congolese refugee who came to the Central African Republic as a child, “Congo Boy” is his story told through fiction, according to the director. “It’s the story of the year my parents went to prison — the year I found myself alone with four younger siblings and forced to find a way to survive. The year music became my lifeline. Everything that happens in the film really happened to me.” In telling his story, Fariala hoped to encourage audiences “to see refugees differently” and to illustrate that “there is a light at the end of the tunnel,” the director previously told Variety . A four-country co-production, “Congo Boy” is produced by Makongo Films, based in the Central African capital of Bangui, Unité in France, the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Kiripifilms and Karta Film in Italy. Paris-based The Party Film Sales is handling “Congo Boy” internationally. The film has sold across Europe and beyond, including such major territories as Germany and Austria, where it will be released by Immergute Filme, France via Jour2fête, and Brazil, where Ipecine is distributing. “Congo Boy” follows Fariala’s award-winning 2022 debut feature, “We, Students!” which bowed in Berlin. The documentary captures the everyday life of the director and his fellow students at the Central African Republic’s Bangui University. title: Hershey Hopes Katseye Will Lure Younger Snackers to New Crème Bars
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:00am PT Hershey Hopes Katseye Will Lure Younger Snackers to New Crème Bars By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest NBC Sends Football on Cross-Country Trip to Count Down to NFL Kickoff 1 hour ago Sony Aims to Connect Advertisers to PlayStation Users With Launch of ‘Live TV on PS5’ (EXCLUSIVE) 22 hours ago Antonia Hylton’s New MS NOW Weekend Show ‘The Assignment’ Debuts September 12 24 hours ago See All Courtesy of Hershey's At The Hershey Company, the candy is the star, but marketing executives at the chocolate titan have figured out a way for the sweets to share screen time with some notable guests. Katseye , the popular all-girl pop group, will have a significant role in a new ad campaign aimed at introducing new Hershey’s Crème Bars to consumers — and their appearance suggests marketers long attached to themes of nostalgia are willing to break some longstanding rules in a bid to get noticed in a crowded marketplace. Related Stories 'Top Boy' Prequel 'Jonny Boy' Starring Barry Keoghan, Jaq Spinoff With Jasmine Jobson Ordered at Netflix What's New on Netflix in September 2026 Hershey’s doesn’t need to do a lot to stand apart. The wrappers for its signature chocolate bar and Reese’s chocolate-and-peanut-butter candy are cultural icons. And yet, the company may need something differ to catch the attention of younger customers, says Stacy Taffet, the company’s chief growth and marketing officer, during a recent interview. Popular on Variety “There’s a lot of trust and nostalgia and emotional connection” tied to Hershey products, Taffet says. “But as we think about a younger cohort, in particular, Gen Z, teens, twenty-somethings, they love Hershey, but they also want to experiment with new flavors, different textures, more indulgent premium experiences.” The new Crème Bars, which come in flavors such as affogato and salted caramel, are meant to stand as something more indulgent, and an alliance with Katseye was seen as a way to nudge a consumer who might not put Hershey in the realm of fancier treats. To emphasize the luxurious nature of the new candy, Katseye sings its song “Pinky Up” in what appears to be the car of a New York subway, with bites of the treat spurring riders to dance and move. The campaign will turn up in streaming video, digital, in national TV, in streaming audio, in social media and on murals in Brooklyn and Los Angeles. Hershey is one of several big candy and snack-makers trying to cultivate younger crowds with new flavors and textures. Ferrara Candy Co., for example, has driven sales by transforming its decades-old Nerds from what were once fruity candy pebbles into candies that have new textures that give consumers a different sort of “mouth feel.” “We are starting to push the boundaries on where our categories can go, thinking about our innovation process,” says Taffet “We are using different types of tools, including AI and social listening to get further ahead of where the consumer is going.” In recent months, Hershey’s has introduced new flavors to Reese’s, including one that pairs the candy with Oreo cookies. The executive says an effort is afoot to enter the lives of a young generation that indulges in what she calls “selective splurging.” Younger consumers “are really intentional in how they spend their dollars. And if they’re going to spend money on something, it’s going to be for an experience that they think is special relative to other things they could spend their money on,” says Taffet. If there’s an extra dollar to be spent, it’s “going to go to something that’s a little bit more special and bring something new that they haven’t experienced before. That bar is high, but I think it’s inspiring us” to try new methods. title: Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen Launches Out of Pocket Studios

The Buffalo Bills quarterback is launching Out of Pocket NFL MVP and star quarterback of the Buffalo Bills, has announced the launch of Out of Pocket Studios , a media venture that will have him backing entertainment, commercial and experiential projects. Allen will serve as CEO of the new company and as an executive producer on all work. Related Stories 'You' Author Caroline Kepnes Sets Series Directorial Debut With Psychological Thriller 'The Attentionist' (EXCLUSIVE) 'Top Boy' Prequel 'Jonny Boy' Starring Barry Keoghan, Jaq Spinoff With Jasmine Jobson Ordered at Netflix The new production outlet builds on an alliance Allen struck Skydance Sports , part of Paramount Skydance, in January of last year. Lindsey Cohen, president of strategy and operations at Out of Pocket Studios, will oversee the company’s day-to-day operations. She previously served at Meadowlark Media and DAZN, and began her career at CAA. “Skydance Sports has given me a platform to turn the ideas I care most about into something real,” said Allen, in a prepared statement. “We’re excited to share what Out of Pocket Studios has created so far, and for everyone to see what we’re building from here.” Popular on Variety The new studio’s initial slate includes “America’s Tailgate,” a TV special slated to air Labor Day on Paramount’s CBS. The program, which will feature music and celebrities, is produced with Skydance Sports, EverWonder Studio, and Lost Tribe Studio, and is hosted by “CBS Mornings” anchor and “The NFL Today” studio analyst Nate Burleson, along with co-host Melanie Collins and correspondent Whitney Cummings. Allen makes an appearance as well. Also set to launch is “NFL Play Action,” a weekly football-analysis studio show is slated to debut on Paramount+ on September 9. The show is hosted by by Kyle Brandt and co-hosted by fitness instructor Ally Love. The pair offer a weekly cultural recap of NFL action in a program meant to spur family viewing. “The Buffalo Miracle” is directed by documentarian Ben Proudfoot and produced with Breakwater Studios and Skydance Sports,. The film captures the heroism of a McDonald’s manager in Buffalo who, during a deadly blizzard in 2022, opened the restaurant to stranded citizens on Christmas Eve. Other projects, including a comedy series conceived by Allen that has already been sold, is in the company’s content pipeline. Both Allen and Out of Pocket Studios are represented by CAA. title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Trailer: Netflix’s Oscar Contender Is a Time-Bending Queer Epic That Won Best Director at Cannes
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 7:00am PT ‘La Bola Negra’ Trailer: Netflix’s Oscar Contender Is a Time-Bending Queer Epic That Won Best Director at Cannes By Mya Copeland Plus Icon Mya Copeland Latest Everything We Know About ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ 4 days ago Hooters Restaurant Movie in the Works — Film News in Brief 4 days ago ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Gameplay Trailer Shows Weapons Destroying Planet in the Series’ Finale (Gaming News Roundup) 5 days ago See All 'La Bola Negra' Carla Oset/Netflix Netflix released the official trailer for “ La Bola Negra ” (“The Black Ball”), from directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi. Set in 1932, 1937 and 2017, the Spanish-language queer epic explores the interconnected lives of three gay men. The film is inspired by an unfinished work of the same name by Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca and Alberto Conejero’s play “La Piedra Oscura” (“The Dark Stone”). Conejero co-wrote the screenplay with Calvo and Ambrossi, known collectively as Los Javis. Related Stories 'Who Has Time to Watch All This Crap?': Inside 10 Anonymous Emmy Ballots as Voting Officially Closes Netflix Teen Thriller 'The Body’ Sets November Release Date, Drops First Look Photos (TV News Roundup) The cast features Spanish musician Guitarricadelafuente (Álvaro Lafuente Calvo) in his acting debut as Sebastián, Carlos González as Alberto, Miguel Bernardeau as Rafael Rodríguez Rapún, Milo Quifes as Carlos, Lola Dueñas as Teresa, Penélope Cruz as Nené Romero, Glenn Close as Isabelle Durand, Julio Torres as Juan Pablo and Alberto Cortés as Federico García Lorca. Popular on Variety The film made its world premiere at Cannes in May, where Calvo and Ambrossi won the Best Director Award. It features an original song, “La Nieve,” written and performed by Guitarricadelafuente, and a score from Raül Refree. “La Bola Negra” is slated for a theatrical release in Spain on Sept. 25. Netflix won the bidding war for U.S. distribution rights following the film’s Cannes premiere and set a theatrical window starting Oct. 16 before a streaming debut on Dec. 2. This marks the longest theatrical window for a Netflix film, breaking the record previously held by 2019’s “Marriage Story” starring Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver. “La Bola Negra” is a Movistar Plus+ Original Film in collaboration with Suma Content Films. Telefónica Audiovisual Digital and Los Esquiadores AIE produced the film. El Deseo and Le Pacte co-produced, with the participation of Atresmedia and CREA SGR. Watch the trailer below. title: ProgCore & Gungnir Form Fantasy Label Alongside Slate Of TV Shows & Podcasts
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Hearst Networks Orders Lizzie Borden & Aileen Wuornos Docs From ‘Ed Gein: Original Psychopath’ Team Edward Berger & Jane Tranter Among Headliners At New-Look MIA ‘Doctor Who’ On Prime Video? Amazon Execs Say They “Welcome Any Conversation Around IP” View All September 1, 2026 7:00am ProgCore founders David Nett and Todd Stashwick and 'Dark Age of Theer' ProgCore EXCLUSIVE: Todd Shastwick and David Nett’s ProgCore , LLC has formed a fantasy imprint with L.A. boutique publisher Gungnir , as they work up a slate of TV and podcast projects. The two companies have joined forces to form ProgCore Press, which will focus on fantasy and roleplaying games and sit within Gungnir’s suite of publishing businesses. To this point, Gungnir has focused on superheroes, science fiction, and fantasy storytelling, and the deal with ProgCore will expand this into dark fantasy and sword and sorcery IP. In return, ProgCore gets access to Gungnir’s distribution network, including its agreement with Macmillan Publishers. Related Stories News Animated Horror-Comedy Series 'Doomsweepers' In Works From 'Monkie Kid' Director Sarah Harper, Flying Bark & Lightfold News Comics Publisher Gungnir Readies "Chaotic" YouTube Comedy Series 'Badd, Gramm-mar' Set Around L.A. Book Club Gungnir and ProgCore are already planning a fantasy roleplaying game-themed cocktail book, a graphic novel and book of short stories set in Theer, and several adventure modules for table-top roleplaying games (TTRPGs) such as Dungeons & Dragons and Shadowdark . Watch on Deadline First up is ProgCore Fantasy: Dark Age of Theer , a 300-page resource for fantasy roleplaying gamers, featuring tips and advice, a detailed description of the original World of Theer, and more than 20 short stories set in Theer from the likes of Bhimani, Wil Wheaton, Terry Matalas, Cecil Castellucci, Bernardin, Erol Otus and Jasmine Bhullar. Hand-designed by Nett, it includes over 150 pieces of original art, and signed, limited editions sold out quickly in March 2026. Initial distribution of this first edition will begin this fall, with an expected retail release spring 2027. This comes as ProgCore develops a proof-of-concept production for an animated series titled Passing Shimmer , which will feature the voice talents of Stashwick and Anjali Bhimani among others. The company is also in post-production on a ten-part “streaming documentary-style RPG actual play” called ProgCore Fantasy: City of Sorrow , which features the likes of Shastwick, Nett, Bhimani, Felicia Day, Yuri Lowenthal, Drea Letamendi and Marc Bernadin. It is in development on “several” sci fi/fantasy and narrative-driven podcasts. ProgCore’s founders have extensive TV and film backgrounds. Stashwick is an actor, writer and teacher, who is currently co-writer on the Skydance Games’ Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra. As an actor, his roles as Captain Liam Shaw in Star Trek: Picard and Deacon in 12 Monkeys and he has upcoming role as Paladin in Marvel’s VisionQuest . He is a central figure in the TTRPG world. Nett’s is known for indie TV series Gold in 2008 and Night of the Zombie King two years later. He has created and contributed to streaming shows for Geek & Sundry, Shout!, Caffeine and others, and ran an L.A. theater company, Lucid by Proxy, for 15 years. “Discovery is forever the enemy of independent art,” said Nett. “With five books, a documentary series, an animated short, two albums, a podcast, and more planned for the next few years, we’re great at making beautiful things on indie budgets, but getting word about our art to the people who will enjoy it is a huge challenge. The partnership with Gungnir gives us the marketing and distribution reach to get our books in front of audiences everywhere.” “Gungnir was built to kick doors open for bold creators and worlds that refuse to play it safe,” said Gungnir CEO Matt Medney. “Todd, David, and ProgCore speak that same language. ProgCore Press is what happens when two fiercely independent creative houses decide to make some noise together. title: ‘Down the Arm of God’ Review: Caleb Landry Jones Finds That God’s House Isn’t a Home in a Stirring Social Drama
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:58am PT ‘Down the Arm of God’ Review: Caleb Landry Jones Finds That God’s House Isn’t a Home in a Stirring Social Drama The actor-writer reteams with his 'To the Night' director Peter Brunner for a moving if slightly schematic story of a Texas priest battling small-town prejudice to help the unhoused. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Sacred Creatures’ Review: Slippery Canadian-Italian Satire Follows the Cult and Collapse of a Questionable Guru 17 hours ago ‘Call My Agent! The Movie’ Review: Love-Hate Energy Keeps the Gang Together in a Fast, Funny Feature-Length Return 2 days ago ‘Sea of Glass’ Review: A Widow’s Coastal Healing Retreat Turns Into a Stately, Moody Greek Tragedy 2 days ago See All Courtesy of Kinology A harvester of disease in “Antiviral,” a white supremacist in “Get Out,” mass murderer Martin Bryant in “Nitram,” Vlad the Impaler himself in “Dracula”: Caleb Landry Jones has carved such a niche for himself playing men not to be touched with a ten-foot pole that “ Down the Arm of God ” immediately stands out for casting the actor as a man of regular, common decency. The takeaway, however, from this affectingly earnest social drama is that decency is neither common nor regular in an increasingly divided, individualist America — something that Jones’ character, small-town Texas priest Nick, learns to his growing anguish. Related Stories Emilia Jones to Star in Netflix Series Adaptation of 'The Retrievals' Podcast Christian Metal Band Demon Hunter Sues Netflix Over 'KPop Demon Hunters,' Citing Trademark Infringement Reteaming the star with Austrian director Peter Brunner , “Down the Arm of God” presents an unsurprisingly skeptical outsider’s view of the land of the free in the MAGA era — its foundational democratic values compromised by desperate economic inequality and bitter ongoing conflicts of race and class. With a diverse ensemble mixing name actors and non-professionals, the film’s first half recalls documentary-infused observational drama in the mold of early Chloé Zhao, as it follows Nick’s efforts to engage with a homeless community on the edge of his parish. Popular on Variety The second, segueing into violently heated, politicized melodrama, is less convincing. But the whole thing is kept on track by the worn, steadfast integrity of Jones’ performance: It’s clear that the film, which he co-wrote with Brunner following their work together on 2018’s tense psychodrama “To the Night,” is a passion project for him, to the extent that his own father John has a fleeting but crucial cameo. Following its world premiere in Locarno’s audience-oriented Piazza Grande section, this French-American co-production (Jones’ “Dracula” director Luc Besson is among the producers) should secure arthouse distribution (or a streaming deal) on both sides of the Atlantic. Breakout potential may be curbed by its stolid, downbeat nature. Shooting in a widescreen format that gives ironic grandeur to a squat, featureless town in the Texas Panhandle, DP Peter Flinckenberg is attentive to the piercing, sometimes radiant winter light of the region in the harshest months of the year. There’s a sparse, severe beauty to its unremarkably suburban vistas, with their freeze-dried lawns and stripped, skeletal trees, but mostly you feel the face-slapping cold through the screen. It’s certainly what Nick first notices as a newcomer to the area, having been rather thanklessly assigned there by the Church; his congregation, consisting mostly of superficially polite but insular white Christian conservatives, isn’t all that warm either. But he’s young and keen and persistent, winning over at least some converts with his amiably straight-talking sermon style and his passionate, community-minded charity drives. On the latter front, he concentrates much effort on a settlement of homeless people barely surviving on the town fringes; they’re wary of his interest at first, but eventually accept his help, with idealistic young Black woman Raven (India Marie Cross, a superb discovery) emerging as their uncompromising leader. But Nick learns the limits of his parishioners’ charity when, as the frostiest temperatures set in, he advocates temporarily sheltering them in the town gymnasium or, failing that, the church itself. Met with a wall of combined NIMBYism and racially coded prejudice from the townspeople — with ultra-Aryan couple Anna (Mena Suvari) and Chris (Nick Stahl) his most hostile opponents — Nick overrides their will and moves the homeless into the house of God anyway. Cue an increasingly fraught war of words — and, eventually and inevitably, other very American weapons — in the congregation, with even the good preacher tiring of turning the other cheek. To begin with, Brunner and Jones’ script brims with patient, generous human interest, abetted by the director’s sure touch with actors of all abilities: Early scenes find hitherto separate demographics sizing each other up and marking out common ground. As it progresses, however, issues and characters alike grow more polarized, in ways that make the film persuasive as polemic — and as an eminently worthy PSA, concluding with a series of title cards about America’s wider homelessness crisis — but slightly less interesting as drama. Beset with inner demons and scarring family tragedy, Nick is a consistently compelling protagonist, but wants for an antagonist of equivalent nuance and complexity: He’d already be on the side of the angels even if the likes of Anna and Chris weren’t such flatly hateful stereotypes. Still, this urgent, moving film is very much a work of its fractious era, when the time taken to see your opponent’s side might come at the expense of someone more worthy of grace. ‘Down the Arm of God’ Review: Caleb Landry Jones Finds That God’s House Isn’t a Home in a Stirring Social Drama Reviewed online, Aug. 31, 2026. title: Gal Gadot Says ‘Wonder Woman 3’ Getting Axed and Henry Cavill’s Superman Exit Were ‘Not Handled Elegantly’ by the Studio but ‘We’re All Adults and It’s All Good’
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:48am PT Gal Gadot Says ‘Wonder Woman 3’ Getting Axed and Henry Cavill’s Superman Exit Were ‘Not Handled Elegantly’ by the Studio but ‘We’re All Adults and It’s All Good’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Gal Gadot Defends Starring in Movie With AI Sets and Lighting Because ‘You’re Going to Work With It or Be Out of the Game’; Lawyers Spent 6 Months Ensuring AI Would Not Alter Actors 16 hours ago Mel Gibson Apologizes for Mocking Sign Language Interpreter as Backlash Grows: ‘Thoughtless Idiocy’ With ‘No Intended Maliciousness’ 20 hours ago John Galliano Cancels Met Gala and Exhibit for 2027 Amid Backlash Over Past Racism: ‘I Remain Deeply Sorry’ to the ‘Jewish and Asian Communities’ 1 day ago See All ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection Gal Gadot insists DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran told her they would develop “ Wonder Woman 3″ with her returning in the title role after they took over the company and rebooted Zack Snyder’s DC Universe. When asked on the latest “Happy Sad Confused” podcast if Gunn and Safran ever told her they would be going in a different direction, Gadot responded: “They told me the opposite! They told me, ‘We’re going to do develop it with you. The third [movie]…'” Related Stories ‘The Gentlemen’ Officially Renewed for Season 3 as First Season 2 Trailer Drops: ‘I’m Looking Forward to Pushing the Boundaries Further,’ Guy Ritchie Says (EXCLUSIVE) Netflix Hires Warner Bros. Exec Katie Martin Kelley as Communications VP Back in 2023, Gadot claimed in interviews with ComicBook.com and Flaunt magazine that Gunn and Safran were interested in developing “Wonder Woman 3.” She told the later publication that she even met with the new heads of DC Studios and “what they told me, and I’m quoting: ‘You’re in the best hands. We’re going to develop “Wonder Woman 3″ with you. [We] love you as Wonder Woman— you’ve got nothing to worry about.’” Sources close to the situation exclusively told Variety at the time that “Wonder Woman 3” was not in development at DC Studios and that nothing was ever promised to Gadot regarding another sequel, nor was there any definitive discussion of Gadot’s Wonder Woman continuing with the new DC Universe. Popular on Variety Gadot originated the role of Wonder Woman in Zack Snyder’s DC Universe, debuting in “Batman v Superman : Dawn of Justice” before leading her own two standalone films: “Wonder Woman” and “Wonder Woman 1984.” Gadot’s Wonder Woman also appeared in “Justice League” and had cameos in DC films such as “Shazam! Fury of the Gods.” Her two standalone “Wonder Woman” films were directed by Patty Jenkins. The two were developing “Wonder Woman 3” together before Gunn and Safran were named the new heads of DC Studios. During her interview on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast, Gadot said she ultimately was not surprised when she got the boot from Wonder Woman because “I saw the way everybody else was handled. The Henry [Cavill] situation was not handled elegantly to say the least. Same with Patty [Jenkins]. It was not handled elegantly. We’re all adults and it’s all good. It’s not even about [James Gunn and Peter Safran]. They are there and they’re there to do what they believe in. It’s all good.” Henry Cavill ‘s return as Superman was officially announced in October 2024 after he returned as the Man of Steel in the “Black Adam” post-credits scene. The announcement was only two months before Gunn and Safran’s DC takeover was officially confirmed, and the duo did not have plans to bring Cavill’s Superman back. Instead, they rebooted “Superman” with David Corenswet. Jenkins, meanwhile, had been developing a third “Wonder Woman” to star Gadot when news broke in December 2022 that their “Wonder Woman 3” had fallen apart after Warner Bros. leadership passed on Jenkins’ treatment for the sequel. Jenkins publicly exited the project. The news hit shortly after James Gunn and Peter Safran took the reins of DC Studios, which led to speculation that Jenkins had rebuffed efforts to reshape “Wonder Woman 3” to fit into their DC Universe. “I never walked away,” Jenkins shared in a post on Twitter at the time. “I was open to considering anything asked of me. It was my understanding there was nothing I could do to move anything forward at this time. DC is obviously buried in changes they are having to make, so I understand these decisions are difficult right now.” Jenkins confirmed on the “Talking Pictures” podcast soon after that her experience with “Wonder Woman” was over “for the time being, easily forever.” “They aren’t interested in doing any ‘Wonder Woman’ for the time being,” Jenkins said. “It’s not an easy task, with what’s going on with DC. James Gunn and Peter Safran have to follow their own heart into their own plans. I don’t know what they are planning on doing or why, so I have sympathy for what a big job it is and they have to follow their heart and do what they’ve got planned.” With her time as Wonder Woman over, Gadot said on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast that she’d likely not return to the role even if the chance arose to make “Wonder Woman 3” again at the new DC Studios. “For me to go to do another Wonder Woman, I am not sure I would at this point in my life with four children and different schools and all of that,” Gadot said. “To check out from all of them for such a long period of time, it doesn’t work for my life anymore at this point.” Watch Gadot’s full interview on the “Happy Sad Confused” podcast in the video below. title: Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to World Premiere at New York Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:40am PT Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to World Premiere at New York Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest Luca Guadagnino’s ‘Artificial’ to World Premiere at New York Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 6 minutes ago Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Triumphs Again in Fourth Weekend With $39 Million, ‘Insidious 6’ Launches to $25 Million 1 week ago ‘The Odyssey’ Beats ‘Deadpool & Wolverine’ as Biggest R-Rated Movie of All Time With $1.35 Billion 2 weeks ago See All New York Film Festival audiences will be the first to see “ Artificial ,” director Luca Guadagnino ‘s movie about OpenAI founder Sam Altman. The buzzy drama, which Neon acquired after Amazon MGM dropped the nearly competed film , will host its world premiere on Oct. 5 at Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall. Guadagnino and the cast, including Andrew Garfield, Monica Barbaro, Yura Borisov, Ike Barinholtz, Cooper Hoffman, Jason Schwartzman and Chris O’Dowd, are expected to attend. Related Stories 'Beef' Creator Lee Sung Jin on Abandoning His Tom Brady Heist Plot and the Finneas, Cailee Spaeny Emmy Snubs YouTube Creator Kevin Langue Is Bringing His Comedy Channels to Netflix “Artificial” stars Garfield as Altman and centers around the tumultuous time when the boss was controversially fired and then rehired by the AI giant. Barbaro plays Open AI’s chief technology officer Mira Murati, Borisov is the OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever who ousts Altman, and Barinholtz portrays Elon Musk. Producers on the movie include David Heyman, Jeffrey Clifford, Guadagnino, Jennifer Fox and Simon Rich. Popular on Variety “Artificial” became one of the buzziest films of the season after Amazon MGM announced in June that the movie would be “better served if it were released by a different studio.” The company’s decision to jettison the project raised more than a few eyebrows around town because it came just a few months after Amazon signed a major partnership with OpenAI, including a $50 billion investment. Plus, Altman attended the wedding of Amazon chief Jeff Bezos in 2025. Multiple studios, including Mubi and Focus, circled “Artificial” before it landed at Neon. “The most remarkable thing about Luca Guadagnino’s sly and sobering new film is that it finds the perfect tone to tell the story of how we arrived at the AI precipice,” says NYFF artistic director Dennis Lim. Artificial traces this trajectory with clear-eyed horror, dark humor, and a sense of existential urgency. If ever there was a movie for its moment, this is it.” Guadagnino’s history with NYFF includes “Call Me by Your Name,” which was a main slate selection, “Bones and All” and “Queer,” which were spotlight selections, and “After the Hunt,” which opened last year’s festival. The 64th edition of New York Film Festival, which takes place from Sept. 25 through Oct. 12, will also feature James Gray’s crime drama “Paper Tiger,” starring Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller; Ava DuVernay’s documentary “14th”; director Tony Gilroy’s music drama “Behemoth!” with Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde and Will Arnett; and Takashi Yamazaki’s kaiju sequel “Godzilla Minus Zero.” Emmy Rossum Says Years-Long ‘Shameless’ Pay Battle Only Ended in Season 8 After Salary Dispute Leaked to the Public: ‘It Was Resolved Within a Day’ American Film Market Expands With Launch of AFM House, Site of Its Innovation Hub William H. title: History Is Paramount: As The Last Warner Bros Merger Trial Proved, A Legal Victory Is No Guarantee Of A Happy Ending
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted History Is Paramount: As The Last Warner Bros Merger Trial Proved, A Legal Victory Is No Guarantee Of A Happy Ending In Latest Threat Of Regulatory Retaliation, Donald Trump Says He’ll Report NBC News’ Kristen Welker To FCC For “Rebuke Or Punishment” ICE Confirms They Have Detained Commentator Milo Yiannopoulos View All September 1, 2026 6:36am Story Arc Attorney Daniel Petrocelli speaks to reporters after winning an antitrust trial for AT&T and Time Warner in 2018 Aaron P. Bernstein/Getty Images The trial was to determine the fate of the Warner Bros empire, with the opposing sides presenting vastly different arguments. The government embraced the market as it has been, while the merging companies pointed to a future marked by disruption. Studio veterans were anxious to get the deal done and cash out, while plenty more who stayed were wary of a culture clash with the new owners. Inside and outside of the company, suspicions abounded about the role of Donald Trump and his animus toward CNN driving the court challenge. Related Stories Legal Paramount-WBD Antitrust Suit Heads To Supreme Court In Red State Vs. Blue State Showdown Over $111B Merger News The ParaBros Backlash: Threats To Leave L.A. & An AG Who Won’t Back Down Divide Hollywood That was the picture eight years ago, when the government sued to block the $85 billion merger of AT&T and Time Warner. The six-week 2018 trial of U.S. vs. AT&T was a showdown billed as a momentous battle between the government and a corporate powerhouse. In 2026, as Paramount jousts with state attorneys general suing on antitrust grounds to stop the $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, the parallels are striking. There are, at the same time, some substantial differences between the Justice Department’s AT&T-Time Warner litigation and the state attorney generals’ lawsuit against the Paramount- WBD deal. AT&T-Time Warner was a vertical transaction and Paramount-WBD is a horizontal one, for starters. A vertical deal, which hasn’t been blocked in the media business for decades, is more difficult to prove as anticompetitive than a horizontal one. Watch on Deadline Both cases, though, highlight just how important one asset is in a fast-changing media environment: time. AT&T and Time Warner won their case resoundingly in 2018, as the judge concluded the government had just not shown the transaction would substantially lessen competition. But the litigation cost the two companies precious time as rivals were building out their streaming platforms. In the end, AT&T cited its deal-related debt burden, at a time of soaring production costs, in opting to exit the entertainment business. (A similarly disastrous takeover of DirecTV cemented the decision, after both mergers cost AT&T shareholders tens of billions of dollars.) In April 2022, a bit less than four years after the Time Warner merger’s close, AT&T spun off the newly named WarnerMedia into a venture with Discovery. Blair Levin, policy analyst at New Street Research, told Deadline via email that the time AT&T lost during the legal quagmire ultimately turned out to be a devastating blow. “While the Trump DOJ had a weak case against AT&T’s purchase (the real cause of which was not traditional Republican antitrust metrics but rather Trump’s anger at CNN), the government was able to delay the deal which was costly to AT&T and diminished the value of the asset,” he said. In the Paramount-WBD case, the states “have a stronger case thank the DOJ against AT&T as it is a horizontal, not a vertical case,” he added. Levin also put a spotlight on the $7 million a day ticking fee for WBD shareholders that Para has to start paying next month and potentially billions more in other costs that could emerge as the parties inch towards the trial next spring. “The litigation is costly to Paramount both because of the ticking fee and the ability of the studios and other assets to engage in deal making while no one is certain who will be in charge when the deals go into production,” he notes. One of the key figures from the AT&T-Time Warner trial is also a prominent player in the Paramount case: Makan Delrahim , the company’s chief legal officer. In 2018, he was the antitrust chief in the Justice Department, and he pushed back at the time on repeated claims of Trump administration influence. Another familiar face is AT&T’s lead attorney, Dan Petrocelli. He is now representing Warner Bros Discovery and is expected to play a supporting role in any trial. The judge in the 2018 case, Richard Leon, was a colorful figure with a penchant for exclamation points, strict rules for gallery decorum (no crossed legs, as all spectators were warned to keep two feet on the floor). He also demonstrated an apparently affinity for Turner Classic Movies, as he more than once asked about its post-merger future. “If there ever were an antitrust case where the parties had a dramatically different assessment of the current state of the relevant market and a fundamentally different vision of its future development, this is the one,” he wrote in one early ruling. “Small wonder it had to go to trial!” Here are some lessons from U.S. vs. AT&T, and why the case matters for Paramount-WBD: Getty Remember, It’s An Antitrust Trial In his opinion, Judge Leon called the trial an “epic battle,” and it certainly seemed so at the time. A Paramount-WBD trial may inspire visions of dramatic showdowns with CEOs on the stand, but journalists’ hopes of such moments quickly come crashing down in the reality of what is at hand: Antitrust trials are dominated by arguments about relevant markets, economic models and their inputs and dueling expert witnesses. They are almost always bench trials, decided by a single judge without the involvement of a jury. Yes, there can be moments where top executives are confronted with embarrassing emails, but most of the time they are wonkish and full of arcane details. That said, Leon did inject some moments of drama, primarily in the way that he announced his decision. Rather than just drop it in the docket, he scheduled a date and time for the announcement, gathered all the parties and the press in the courtroom, and forbid anyone from leaving until he was finished reading portions of his opinion. The 100 or so people packed into the courtroom and dozens more waiting just outside reacted with a frenzy to the news that the deal would close, reshaping Hollywood a bit less than two decades after Time Warner’s ill-fated marriage with AOL. The Future Factor Leon concluded that the government had just failed to show that the AT&T-Time Warner merger would substantially lessen competition. And he devoted considerable portions of his opinion to taking down the government’s chief expert witness and his economic models – which perhaps stands as a warning to the state AGs as they prepare to make their case against Paramount. The judge also acknowledged the fast-changing landscape, noting that in the face of declining video subscriptions and TV ad revenues and the rise of streaming and social media. In seeking to combine, AT&T and Time Warner “concluded that both companies could stop ‘chasing taillights’ and catch up with the competition,” he wrote. One of Paramount’s big arguments nowadays for the WBD merger is that a bulked-up combined entity would create a more robust competitor to Netflix, Amazon and Disney, especially in the streaming world. Among other things, Paramount argues that streaming and theatrical can’t be completely separated from theatrical, and that the merger will create a “virtuous cycle: more theatrical content will drive engagement on the combined streaming platform, a larger subscriber base will generate revenue to fund more theatrical content, and the merged firm will become a stronger competitor to the technology companies atop the streaming market.” The states’ lawsuit doesn’t challenge the merger’s impact on the recently established market of streaming. Rather, it alleges competitive harm in three traditional markets: wide-release theatrical film distribution; anticipated big-budget blockbusters; and cable television channel licensing. The cable market is where there is some overlap between the cases against AT&T and Paramount. Back in 2018, the government argued the combination of AT&T’s distribution and Time Warner’s content would give them more leverage, forcing rivals like Comcast and Charter to pay more in distribution fees for “must have” channels like CNN, TNT and HBO – or even withholding them altogether. In a nod to the future, the government also argued that the combined company would have the power to slow the transition to streaming. The state AGs argue that Paramount will control more than 50 channels, including the most “in-demand” programming, like NCAA March Madness and Major League Baseball, giving it “enormous bargaining power” that will leave distributors with “little choice but to accept onerous terms.”

title: Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson Discusses Industry Challenges, Winning Strategies Ahead of Rendez-Vous Market in Le Havre
full_text: Sep 1, 2026 6:24am PT Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson Discusses Industry Challenges, Winning Strategies Ahead of Rendez-Vous Market in Le Havre 'Hyper-distribution' can be scary, but it is leading to real advantages and increasing the international reach of shows on a wide range of channels and platforms, Pélisson notes By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson Discusses Industry Challenges, Winning Strategies Ahead of Rendez-Vous Market in Le Havre 31 minutes ago Unifrance Rendez-Vous TV Mart Spotlights Ancient Rome, 19th Century Paris, Retired Spooks, Luchadores, Diplomatic Intrigue and Gaza 1 day ago Patricio Valladares Descends Into Hell With Horror Adaptation of Dante’s ‘Inferno’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago See All The French audiovisual sector is gearing up for the Unifrance Rendez-Vous in Le Havre , not only France’s premiere TV programming market but also an industry confab offering a clear assessment of how business trends and global developments are reshaping the domestic playing field, from evolving distribution models to programming increasingly tailored for export. Speaking to Variety ahead of the event, which runs Sept. 7-10 in Normandy’s famed port city, Unifrance President Gilles Pélisson discusses the pressing issues facing French distributors and producers and the continuing strength of local content on the international market. Related Stories Netflix’s Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With 'The Gentlemen' HBO Max Banks on Upcoming Genre Thriller ‘Mataviejitas: The Serial Killer’ (EXCLUSIVE) The changing landscape for French TV distribution in the wake of increasing consolidation and streaming dominance is one major topic du jour that is affecting industries across Europe. Popular on Variety Gilles Pélisson Courtesy of Nicolas Gouhier “French TV distribution is not immune to the turbulence of the international market, and there is real concern among French distributors,” Pélisson points out. “Some critical questions have emerged with everyone watching: What will be the future model of European public broadcasters, how much will the streamers continue to produce locally and buy new programs, and how will private free-to-air channels cope with a shrinking advertising market?” Nevertheless offering an upbeat take, Pélisson stresses that new content is still needed regardless. “This is why we are delighted to welcome once again around 130 buyers to Le Havre this year. We worked with our distributors in June to preview their expectations, and the message is clear: French production keeps offering exceptional diversity, with relevant content for every kind of buyer.” The changing distribution landscape has, in the face of streaming dominance, seen the rise of “hyper-distribution.” Discussing the strategy at last year’s Mipcom, Glance, the TV and video market intelligence division of French audience measurement company Médiamétrie, stated: “[T]he need to distribute content everywhere while collaborating with rivals often creates a winning strategy.” Pélisson agrees: “Hyper-distribution can be scary, yet it’s showing some true benefits. It can clearly expand reach: A hit like ‘ Miraculous ’ can be present simultaneously on a wide range of channels and platforms across many countries, more than what was possible or even thinkable a decade ago. But simple presence does not guarantee to be seen.” Indeed, when the same content is available everywhere simultaneously, “it can disappear into the catalogue just as easily as it can stand out,” Pélisson emphasizes. “This is why, alongside our sales data, Unifrance tracks not only where French programs are distributed but how they actually perform, with data such as audience market share or viewed hours.” Continued analysis and receiving as much data as possible from all players is therefore crucial, he adds. “Quality programs can only be made if there is money to produce them!” Turning to the international appetite for French content, the Unifrance chief notes that Europe remains its core market, “and where the momentum is the most solid.” Poland, in particular, has become a leading territory this year as the top country for broadcasts of French programs on linear channels, while Germany remains a leading territory “thanks to a rich offering on the streaming side.” Despite reports that global audiences are moving away from Hollywood content , Pélisson remains cautious. “Buyers are certainly more risk-averse and negotiations may take longer, which leads some players towards proven, well-known IP,” he explains. “Nevertheless, the appetite for a strong non-English alternative is real, and France is very well positioned to answer.” ‘Grizzy & the Lemmings’ Courtesy of Studio Hari He adds: “All genres travel well — that’s the strength of the French offering. Animation remains our flagship in terms of sheer volume on foreign linear channels, carried by evergreen franchises like ‘Miraculous’ and ‘Grizzy & the Lemmings.’” The story is different on streaming, however, where fiction leads the way and, in value terms, drama has become France’s leading export genre over the last two years. Documentary, meanwhile, remains “a strong, steady genre, with real festival and platform presence.” Looking at emerging markets, Pélisson points out that “it is more about volume than value: buyers are very price-sensitive and increasingly digital-driven, so animation and formats do well there.” Overall, animation leads the way in global sales, “with ‘Miraculous’ enjoying by far the widest international footprint of any French title, alongside strong travelers like ‘Grizzy & the Lemmings’ and the ‘ Totally Spies! ’ revival.” ‘The Bureau’ Courtesy of Federation Entertainment On the fiction side, Pélisson notes that older titles are still doing well abroad: Federation ’s hit espionage thriller “The Bureau” has continued its remarkable international journey, while series like Studio TF1 ’s profiler crime drama “Profilage” (“The Paris Murders”) and Film & Pictures’ mystery miniseries “Un Soupçon” (“The Black Widow”) have found substantial audiences on major channels and platforms across Europe. ‘Miyazaki: The Spirit of Nature’ Courtesy of Les Bons Clients Among documentary shows that have reached strong global audiences on streaming are Balanga’s “Miyazaki: The Spirit of Nature,” about Oscar-winning animator and filmmaker Hayao Miyazaki, and Netflix ’s “Tour de France.” Despite an increasingly challenging environment, animation remains France’s top audiovisual export due to a number key factors, Pélisson says. “French animation rests on sound foundations: world-class studios, a training pipeline which is the envy of the sector, and a catalogue of IP with real brand equity. “This being said, we have been seeing sales decline for a year now, for two main reasons. First, streamers — and French broadcasters too — are ordering fewer new projects and fewer new IPs. Secondly, the major streamers take a global approach when producing.” Pélisson points to Netfix’s “Asterix & Obelix: The Big Fight” as an example. “When a global streamer produces the series, the entire international value is folded into a single production figure that counts as financing for a French production, not as an export sale. This is exactly why data matters so much — the only way to know what a program is really worth, on an international basis, would be to separate the value of its national exposure from its international one. Therefore, part of our real international success simply does not appear in the figures, both on the sales and audiences sides.” Animation producers are likewise finding ways to better navigate the tougher market. “Producers are leaning into exactly what makes the sector resilient — building franchises rather than one-off titles, accelerating co-productions to share risk, and designing for both linear and streaming distribution from the outset,” Pélisson explains. ‘Robin Hood: Mischief in Sherwood’ Courtesy of Mediawan Kids & Family Among the new and returning shows that are dazzling audiences abroad are Banijay Kids & Family’s “ Totally Spies!” revival, which “has found a genuinely global audience”; and, from Mediawan Kids & Family, “Robin Hood: Mischief in Sherwood,” which “keeps expanding its territory count”, and the “Miraculous” universe, which “continues to extend across formats.” “The winning formula, Pélisson adds, “is a strong brand that can live across many windows at once — which is precisely where the market is heading.” American Film Market Expands With Launch of AFM House, Site of Its Innovation Hub William H. title: Leslie Odom Jr. Reveals Documentary About His  ‘Hamilton’ Return & Talks Original Cast Reunions
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Nada Aboul Kheir Nada Aboul Kheir Social Media Manager More Stories By Nada Sam Mendes’ Beatles Production Heading For Abbey Road Shoot ‘The Odyssey’: Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson & Travis Scott Hit The Red Carpet For World Premiere In London Cate Blanchett’s Displacement Film Fund To Support Short Films By Mo Amer, Annemarie Jacir, Rithy Panh, Akuol de Mabior & Bao Nguyen View All September 1, 2026 6:00am Leslie Odom Jr. in 'Hamilton' at the Victoria Palace Theatre Danny Kaan EXCLUSIVE: The inimitable, original Leslie Odom Jr. could be found in London this summer for his West End debut, where he reprised the role of Aaron Burr in Hamilton at the Victoria Palace Theatre for nine weeks – and now we can reveal he’s making a documentary about his return to the Broadway version. Odom Jr. is the only original cast member from Lin-Manuel Miranda ’s Pulitzer Prize-winning musical to perform on the UK side of the pond. Deadline was in the room where it happens on August 6, which was coincidentally the star’s birthday, as well as the 11 th anniversary of Hamilton ’s official opening on Broadway in 2015. Related Stories News Acclaimed, Controversial Play 'Downstate' Gets Broadway Marquee; Scott Rudin Reportedly Producing With Joe Mantello Directing Reviews 'Paranormal Activity' Broadway Review: Stage Adaptation Of Film Franchise Is A Frightfully Good Time View this post on Instagram I sat two rows behind Scary Spice aka Mel B, who told me that she’s seen the show “loads of times,” and had a great time with her daughter that night. She wasn’t the only one. As soon as the Tony and Grammy Award-winner walked on stage to start off the show, the energy in the theater shifted. The applause barely stopped, and the crowd sang along to every word as well as danced in their seats throughout the entire two-and-a-half-hour show. “Normally, you’re opening a new show and you’re worried before the curtain goes up, said Odom Jr. about the West End audience. “But in this situation, the people are as excited as I am, if not more.” A few weeks later, after a matinee performance, the Oscar-nominee joined a Zoom call from the Victoria Palace stalls to chat about the West End experience, his willingness to be vulnerable to tap into Burr, a new “really beautiful” documentary about his return to Hamilton on Broadway, original cast reunions and more. “There was a little film crew that made a documentary about me going back into the show in New York, which will be out soon enough,” revealed Odom Jr. during our call. “I’m pretty proud of it and the way it’s coming together. Ten years is a special marker.” The film is set to be submitted to film festivals in the fall. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. DEADLINE: You’re now eight weeks into your nine-week run in the West End. How would you reflect on your experience? What were the highlights and the challenges? LESLIE ODOM JR: It was everything that I hoped it would be. These are hallowed spaces. They’re legendary houses, and to get to have nine weeks at the Victoria Palace was everything I dreamt it would be. I have loved every single moment. I couldn’t have asked for a better debut than Hamilton . Normally, you’re opening a new show and you’re worried before the curtain goes up. But in this situation, which is maybe once in a lifetime, the people are as excited as I am, if not more. So, it’s been wonderful. For challenging moments, I’ll say eight shows a week ain’t for punks. It is more than a notion. That is always challenging, and the West End was no different. I did get ill during one show and it made headlines, which I hated. I’ve never had that happen before. Other than that, I’ve been able to be here every show and that is always the greatest challenge. With this show in particular, it is a crazy equation. You get even more than you put into it. Somehow, at the end of every week, I am more filled up than when I started. I’m exhausted, but I’m also exhilarated. DEADLINE: I watched the show on your birthday a few weeks ago, and the reaction in the room was electrifying – especially when you walked in during “Wait for It,” and “Room Where It Happens.” After performing in hundreds of Hamilton shows, do you always know what to expect from the audience reactions, or do they sometimes surprise you? ODOM JR: Never. I try not to expect anything from an audience. My philosophy is that the collective is always correct. Whatever is in the room for them, however they respond, it is always right. I don’t blame them, I don’t judge them, that’s not my business. I asked them to be here. I said I was coming, and they showed up. That’s the contract. I show up, you show up, and whatever happens in the room is okay by me. They surprise me all the time with the things that they do and don’t respond to. They’ve taught me how to perform this material. They’ve taught me about love and acceptance. They’ve been a sort of guide as I have developed a deeper relationship and love for myself over the last 10 years. I’m so thankful to these audiences. DEADLINE: Speaking of the past 10 years and how things have evolved, I’m curious about how your approach to playing Burr has changed. I’ve watched the show on Disney+ many times, but I noticed that you’ve added some extra humor to the character in certain scenes during the live show. Did you consciously want to make those changes this time around, or did it come naturally? ODOM JR: It’s all coming up naturally. I am in a more joyful space in my life, and the show is worth celebrating. It started out with a very small group of us that loved this show before anybody had even heard it, and now it has rang out around the world. It connected with audiences, people young and old, the world over. That’s worth celebrating. It is so joyful. I don’t step on this stage most nights without thinking of the first time I stepped on a professional stage, which was with the Broadway company of Rent . I think of that kid and how proud he is of the life we’ve built, and that a way has been made for him to exist in the world just as he is. An audience has accepted him, lifts him up each night, and applauds some nights just because he came to work. He is so proud every single day, and so filled with gratitude. I’m in touch with him, so I can tell you. You feel the joy emanating off me because joy is the only thing that is left 10 years later. DEADLINE: Let’s talk a bit about the cultural impact of Hamilton . When it first debuted, Lin-Manuel Miranda described it as “The story of America then, told by America now.” But after all these years, it has surpassed that and has become even more significant globally. Why do you think it affects people so much? Especially the non-Americans? ODOM JR: There is a mystery to it that humbles me, and I think that it’s always meant to. If I came on here and told you exactly what it is about this show that has moved audiences in this way, then it’s something that can be replicated, once or twice a year. There would be more Hamilton s. There’s something miraculous about it. I don’t totally understand what people see when they watch us performing this work. Maybe they see something that makes them feel a little more alive. I’m kind of applying what meaningful theatrical experiences have done for me. They made me feel more alive. They made me feel more seen. They made me feel like I wanted to be a better version of myself. Maybe that’s what people are getting. DEADLINE: How do you make the so-called villain of Hamilton ’s story become one of the most loved characters in theatre? ODOM JR: I don’t judge him for his humanity. It’s his ridiculousness, short-sightedness and willingness to be vulnerable. Lin wrote him that way – vulnerable. When I step on a stage, I start telling a story, right? There’s vulnerability in that. It’s counterintuitive. In life, sometimes vulnerability is the last thing we want to be because it’s scary. This is yet another thing that I’ll take with me from this experience. Because at the beginning, I too was worried that people would hate me. I was like, ‘My God, I’m gonna stand on stage with Lin-Manuel Miranda and people are gonna despise me, and that’s gonna be so hard to feel every night.’ But my willingness to be despised and to be true led to this warm embrace that I get now all over the world, not just in New York. It’s a profound lesson that I’ll be able to teach my kids. I can be more vulnerable and honest in my life. I will find people for whom that’s okay. You can find your room, the places in this world where people might just applaud for it. They might encourage that and love you exactly for who you are. DEADLINE: When you came back to this role after such a long time, were there any songs that required more preparation than others in rehearsals? Or any that threw you off a little bit? ODOM JR: Oh, for sure! I have a lot of those moments. (Laughs and hums the first beat of “Alexander Hamilton”) . If I mistakenly go to a wrong rhythm or insert a wrong word; it’s a hard train to get back on once you’re off. It’s just the way Lin wrote it. That was difficult. Breath control and conditioning took a little while. Actually, there was a little film crew that made a documentary about me going back into the show in New York, which will be out soon enough. I’m pretty proud of it and the way it’s coming together. Ten years is a special marker. The director that made the film said something like, ‘We change far less in a year than we think, and in 10 years, we change more than we realize.’ DEADLINE: When is the film going to come out? ODOM JR: We’re submitting to festivals this fall. So, hopefully we’ll do the festival circuit, then somebody will be interested, and it’ll be on a streamer somewhere or in a movie theatre. It’s really beautiful. It’s a beautiful time, a beautiful season, and somebody sat outside of it and put a frame around it. There are moments that I’ll cherish from that film. Moments with me and my kids, and the new cast. They turned it into art. It was these beautiful moments in my life that they made into something more than that. DEADLINE: Does it have a name yet? ODOM JR: We’re going back and forth about names. It doesn’t have a name that we can all agree on yet. DEADLINE: You’ve come back to Hamilton twice in the past year , and Christopher Jackson is reprising his role as George Washington on Broadway soon. Have there been any discussions about bringing back the full original cast for a couple shows or a tour? ODOM JR: We have legitimate stars in our cast now. There’s Academy Award winners and nominees, so, I think that the scheduling would be too insane at this point. The best we can hope for are these little step-in moments, when people can clear their schedules to come in the show and revisit. I’ll certainly be going to see Chris and whoever else steps into the role. Maybe some people will go into different roles. I’ve always wanted to see [Anthony] Ramos as Hamilton. I think he would be insane. Wouldn’t he be great? DEADLINE: That would be a great casting, actually! You’re also going on tour in Europe for the first time, and working on a horror movie about Sammy Davis Jr. How are you managing your time with everything coming up? ODOM JR: We’re getting ready for the Christmas tour. We’ll start rehearsals for that in November. But before that, I’m going to come back and do some European dates. We’ve never done that before. It’s solely based off the strength of Hamilton and the response that these eight or nine weeks have had in Europe. It’s made it possible that when tickets went on sale in Paris, they were sold out in 10 minutes. I’ve never played Paris so, that is deeply meaningful. They added a second show here in London, in Paris and some other places. We want to build that relationship. We want to come back to Europe for Christmas. They have Christmas all over the world. This is just the beginning. It’s probably the last time I’m going to do Hamilton in London, but I hope it won’t be the last time that I come to London. We’ve got music, movies and lots of stuff. title: Howard Stern Hands Over One SiriusXM Channel to Andy Cohen
full_text: Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 5:00am Howard Stern and Andy Cohen on Sirius XM Courtesy of Sirius XM Howard Stern is officially handing over one of his SiriusXM channels to Andy Cohen starting Sept. 1. The transition comes about one year after Stern and Cohen pranked listeners by having Cohen take over the airwaves and imply that Stern was fired and that Howard 100, Stern’s main channel, was now his own. The prank came amid rumors about Stern’s impending retirement and the cancellation of his show. This time, Stern is actually giving Cohen Channel 101, his second channel which hosted archival clips of his show, as he returns and transitions to only doing one show a week, rather than the typical two. Stern has also struck a deal with HBO Max to adapt his live SiriusXM show into streaming episodes for HBO Max. “Last year we pranked the world. We made everybody think that I was taking over Howard 100. It was the best morning. Now the carrot is being dangled that Radio Andy will be taking over 101. Is this a prank? Am I being pranked?” Cohen asks Stern in a new video released by SiriusXM. “No, you are not being pranked. And Andy has been gracious enough to take over 101. And I have one request: please continue the tradition of doing a lot of gay antics,” Stern says. On Sept. 14, Howard will also unveil a new lineup for his Howard 100 channel, which will include Wrap Up Wednesday , an expanded version of Howard’s Wrap Up Show hosted by Gary Dell’Abate and Jon Hein that previously ran on Howard 101. In the past, Cohen, who helms a SiriusXM radio empire, including hosting Andy Cohen Live, has been rumored to be the eventual successor for Stern. SiriusXM did not comment on that theory, but Cohen and Stern seemed to downplay the idea. “Any chance I could get 100, and you take 101?” Cohen asks in the video. “No, I’m not giving up 100,” Stern says. As part of the channel shakeup, Sebastian Maniscalco’s Comedy Radio will take over Cohen’s previous channel, 102, while Netflix is a Joke Radio will move to channel 105, which has been home to temporary or pop-up programming. SiriusXM did not comment on reported layoffs as part of Stern’s move to one show a week. THR

title: Fewer Women Are Creating TV Shows Now Than They Were Nearly a Decade Ago, Study Finds
full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 5:00am Rachel Sennott, creator and star of 'I Love LA' season one, which premiered in 2025. Kenny Laubbacher/HBO The number of women working as TV creators and directors on original U.S. shows airing on streaming services has declined, in addition to female characters in major roles, according to the latest “Boxed In” study released Tuesday. The report, which tracked over 2,500 characters and more than 3,600 behind-the-scenes credits during the 2025-26 television year, was penned by Dr. Martha Lauzen, executive director of the Center for the Study of Women in Television and Film at San Diego State University. She found that the amount of women creating shows across streaming plummeted from 36 percent in 2024-25 to 24 percent in 2025-26, which was a stark contrast to the increase the year prior (27 percent in 2023-24 to 36 percent in 2024-25). The new findings indicate that last year’s increases were a momentary surge, rather than the beginning of a positive trend. As for broadcast, women creators also declined slightly from 20 percent in 2024-25 to 19 percent in 2025-26. “The numbers of women creating shows on both platforms are now lower than they were almost a decade ago in 2017-18,” Lauzen said. When it came to the percentage of women directing streaming projects, the report found that number also dropped from 32 percent in 2024-25 to 22 percent in 2025-26, following the temporary increase after 2023-24 (23 percent). Women directing broadcast programs also dipped from 18 percent in 2024-25 to 16 percent in 2025-26. This new study follows a report from The Hollywood Reporter in June that spotlighted the lack of progress in women-held below-the-line positions after a behind-the-scenes video of Sydney Sweeney on the set of Euphoria season three started circulating on social media. At the time, fans were quick to point out that the majority of the crew members seen in the clip were men, while Sweeney was sitting in a suggestive pose. As for roles in front of the camera, the number of female characters in major roles also declined last year, per the study. For streaming, women comprised 44 percent of major characters in 2025-26, down from 49 percent in 2024-25, and on broadcast, females accounted for 46 percent of major characters, down slightly from 47 percent in 2024-25. The report also found that male characters continue to have an easier time aging on television compared to female characters. On both streaming and broadcast shows, the majority of women in speaking roles were in their 20s and 30s, while the majority of men were in their 30s and 40s. The number of female characters also experienced a steep decline as they aged from their 30s into their 40s, while their male counterparts didn’t experience a substantial drop until their 50s. “The emphasis on youth for the majority of female characters foregrounds their appearance, whereas males are able to credibly age into positions of personal and public power, normalizing the perception that men are naturally more powerful than women,” Lauzen added. “The fully-realized characters played by Kathy Bates on Matlock or Jean Smart on Hacks remain the exception, not the rule, for women on television.” The “Boxed In” report has monitored over 65,000 characters and more than 80,00 behind-the-scenes credits on original dramas, comedies and reality television programs over the last 27 years, starting in 1997-98. It aims to provide a comprehensive historical record of women’s representation and employment in television. THR

title: ‘Tomb Raider’ Series Broke UK Safety Laws During Production
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake StudioCanal’s ‘Has Fallen’ Series Returns For Season 3; Iwan Rheon, Brendan Coyle & Atandwa Kani Cast Inside ‘The Great British Bake Off’ Bun Fight: How Sky & Love Productions Came To Blows Over The UK’s Biggest Cooking Series Edinburgh TV Festival Diary: Farewell To The Great City; YouTube Takeover; Channel 4’s Next Content Chief & Paramount Mischief View All September 1, 2026 4:19am Sophie Turner as Lara Croft in 'Tomb Raider' Jay Maidment for Prime Video EXCLUSIVE : Lara Croft’s adventures in Amazon MGM Studios ‘ new Tomb Raider series proved too much for UK safety authorities. Britain’s Health and Safety Executive, better known as HSE, concluded that the high-profile drama breached UK safety laws during production at Shinfield Studios earlier this year, according to a previously unreported ruling. Deadline can reveal that Project Temple Productions Ltd, the special purpose vehicle through which Sophie Turner ‘s Tomb Raider series is being produced, breached the Health and Safety At Work Act 1974 and Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002. Related Stories Casting KiKi Layne & Luke Hemsworth Join Amazon MGM Actioner 'Deadlocked' Casting Sasha Calle Joins Jamie Foxx In Amazon MGM Action Flick 'Deadlocked' Amazon MGM Studios declined to comment. Watch on Deadline HSE determined that Project Temple Productions Ltd failed to ensure that crew members underwent “biological monitoring” to ensure adequate control measures were in place for the spraying of isocyanate paints, one of the leading causes of asthma in the workplace. HSE guidance states that appropriate personal protective equipment should be worn when spraying isocyanate paints, and that an “invisible mist” emitted by the substance can take up to 20 minutes to clear. An employer must know the clearance time for the space in which spraying is taking place. HSE issued Project Temple with an “improvement notice” in April, meaning the company had to take action to remedy a breach of health and safety law. Within a month, Project Temple had complied with the relevant regulations, according to a notice page on HSE’s website. It is rare for HSE to issue notices against TV shoots, with just four productions being called out by the health and safety watchdog over the past four years. Tomb Raider was the highest-profile of these productions. Written by Fleabag creator Phoebe Waller-Bridge , Tomb Raider went into production in January, with Amazon MGM Studios releasing a first-look image of Turner as videogame icon Lara Croft. The HSE ruling has not been the only issue on Tomb Raider . Turner suffered a minor injury during production , resulting in the shoot being paused for around two weeks to allow the Game of Thrones star time to recover. Amazon MGM Studios produces Tomb Raider for Prime Video with Crystal Dynamics. Turner is joined in the cast by Sigourney Weaver, Jason Isaacs, Martin Bobb-Semple, Jack Bannon, John Heffernan, Bill Paterson, Paterson Joseph, Sasha Luss, Juliette Motamed, Celia Imrie and August Wittgenstein. Waller-Bridge is creator, writer, executive producer and co-showrunner alongside Chad Hodge as co-showrunner and executive producer. Jonathan Van Tulleken is director and executive producer. Waller-Bridge and Jenny Robins executive produce through Wells Street Films, Dmitri M. Johnson, Michael Lawrence Goldberg and Timothy I. title: Netflix’s New Releases Coming in September 2026
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 4:00am From top left: 'Stavros Halkias: Uncle Stav,' 'Dang!,' NFL Melbourne Game, 'LEGO ONE PIECE,' 'Unabomber,' 'The Gentlemen,' 'Stranger Things: Tales From '85' and 'Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.' Netflix; Gregory Shamus/Getty Images The return Guy Ritchie’s hit comedy crime series The Gentlemen ; an animated Asian-American comedy from Andrew Law; the latest special from comedian-of-the-moment Stavros Halkias ; the much-hyped comeback of Aaron Donald as the NFL heads Down Under for the first-ever regular season game in Australia; a second season of animated tales from 1985 Hawkins, Indiana; the fourth chapter of Ryan Murphy’s Monster anthology series; a two-part Lego animated One Piece special; and Jacob Tremblay depicting the origin story of Unabomber are just some of the film and TV highlights hitting Netflix in September. Related Stories TV 'Tires' Renewed for Season 4 by Netflix TV 'Manifest' Spinoff 'Arrivals' Landing at Netflix In the midst of all the speculation on whether Meghan Markle will be joining season 3 of The Gentlemen , it would have been easy to forget that season 2 of the hit Guy Ritchie comedy crime series launches on Sept. 3. The logline for season 2 reads, “It’s been one year since Eddie and Susie joined forces to work together in Bobby’s criminal empire overseas. As they drive to expand their enterprise, the decisions Bobby is making seem to be increasingly unsound. Now Eddie and Susie must decide whether to take action or risk losing it all.” Theo James, Kaya Scodelario, Daniel Ings, Joely Richardson, Vinnie Jones, Giancarlo Esposito and Ray Winstone all return for the second season, with newcomers including Hugh Bonneville, Benjamin Clementine, Benedetta Porcaroli, Amra Mallassi, Tyler Conti and Chris Eubank Jr. Netflix continues its push into adult animated comedies with the launch of Dang! on Sept. 8. The terminally online will have picked up on the spirited debate the show inspired on social media when a trailer for the Andrew Law-created Asian-American project first dropped. Those who are lucky enough not to be brain-poisoned by internet chatter, maybe interested to know that the show “follows a brother and sister duo whose fun, messy lives in New York City are interrupted when their worst nightmare comes true: their high-achieving older sister shows up and wants to hang out with them.” It’s not much deeper than that, for better or worse. Poppy Liu, Andrew Law, Noël Wells and Stephanie Hsu provide the voices. Stavros Halkias is the comedian-of-the-moment and his fame is only likely to grow with his new Netflix special landing on Sept. 8. Halkias, the former Cumtown podcaster, current star of Netflix comedy Tires as well as scene stealer in films like Bugonia and Tony , is a new breed of standup that’s crude but empathetic, a refreshing change of pace from the Roganverse comics who seem to delight in punching down and being cruel for the sake of it. Uncle Stav is a followup to 2023’s hilarious Fat Rascal , and deals with Halkias becoming an uncle. Sept. 17 will see the debut of the next installment of Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s Emmy-winning anthology series Monster hits Netflix. The eight-episode fourth chapter, The Lizzie Borden Story , is series’ first female-led tale and will focus on the infamous 1892 axe murders of Borden’s father and stepmother in Fall River, Massachusetts. Ella Beatty stars as Lizzie and the stellar cast includes Charlie Hunnam, Vicky Krieps, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden and Sarah Paulson. Also on Sept. 17, we return to Hawkins once more for season 2 of Stranger Things: Tales From ’85. Unsurprisingly, the animated series hasn’t inspired the same level of fervor or expectation as the live-action Stranger Things show did, but there are still millions of fans out there to service with more tales of retro horrors from the Upside Down. The logline for season 2 reads, “With Valentine’s Day on the way, the gang must uncover the truth behind ghostly apparitions and a swarm of strange creatures causing chaos around town.” On Sept. 18, the NFL continues its quixotic attemtps to grow American Football around the world with its first-ever regular season game in Australia, dubbed the NFL Melbourne Game . That’s right, the land of hard-running and hard-hitting Aussie Rules, Rugby Union and Rugby League will host a game of the premiere ball-based stop-start contact sport where you wear full padding and helmets.
