title: Iranian Director Mohsen Gharaei Talks Navigating Censors To Bring Prophetic Drama ‘Falling House’ To Fruition – Venice
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Josh Duhamel To Star In ‘Speak’ From Lorenzo Di Bonaventura & Joe Carnahan; Twenty-Nine Palms & CAA Media Finance Launching Sales At TIFF Zurich Bolsters Position As Awards Circuit Stop-Off As ‘Bunker’, ‘Club Kid’ & ‘Adult Supervision’ Join Gala Lineup TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’ View All September 1, 2026 4:00am Falling House Seven Springs Pictures, RaeFilm Studios EXCLUSIVE: Close to four years have passed since Iran ’s Woman Life Freedom protests were sparked by the death in police custody, on September 16, 2022, of Mahsa Amini following her arrest for not wearing her hijab correctly. In a sign of their lasting impact, Iranian director Mohsen Gharaei arrives in Venice this year with Falling House , a prophetic work warning of the crisis building in Iran after decades of oppressive, patriarchal rule by the Islamic Republic regime. The allegorical drama, which world premieres in Venice’s Orizzonti sidebar, revolves around three generations of women in an economically fragile family, living under the thumb of the father and facing eviction from their long-time home due to an airport expansion project. Related Stories News TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender 'Woman Unknown' Festivals Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down Initially appearing as a kindly, henpecked figure who affords his wife and daughters a fair amount of independence, the father reveals a more sinister side when they challenge his authority. Laleh Marzban, whose credits include the 2023 Iranian Oscar submission The Night Guardian , stars as eldest daughter Ensi, who has hatched a secret plan to move to Turkey to pursue ambitions of becoming a model, opposite award-winning veteran actor Farhad Aslani as her father. Rima Raminfar plays the long-suffering but determined mother, with Elena Khakbaz making her big-screen debut as the youngest daughter, Jenan, who is bullied at school over her father’s job amid claims that he is a prison executioner, but remains a beacon of hope as she challenges obstacles at every turn. A first clip below, showing the family awakening to shaking walls and the rumble of bulldozer engines, captures the sense of a toxic status quo on the verge of collapse that runs throughout the film. Falling House is Gharaei’s first film in five years, following a self-imposed hiatus in response to government restrictions and censorship around filmmaking. He wrote a first draft in 2018 but reveals that it was the 2022 Woman Life Freedom protests that gave him fresh impetus to get the film off the ground. “The protests happened four years later, but the reasons that led society to that point were already there. I’d always wanted to tell this story, but Woman Life Freedom gave me a better and stronger reason to bring it to film,” says Gharaei. The film is one of two Iranian pictures playing in Venice, alongside Ali Asgari’s Golden Lion contender, A Bit Of Light, as Iran remains in the spotlight due to the war with the U.S. and Israel, as well as reports that its ruling Islamic Republic regime continues to persecute and execute pro-democracy dissenters. Prior to his directing hiatus, Gharaei enjoyed box office chart-topping success at home with his respective 2017 and 2021 films, Blockage and Majority , with the latter winning the jury prize at the Islamic Republic regime-controlled Fajr Film Festival. Today, he says he is living in exile, his home and assets confiscated, with him and his family subject to death threats after drawing the regime’s ire with public comments criticizing its conduct in the early days of the U.S. and Israeli bombing campaign in March 2026, and now with his new film. “If I go back, I will definitely face a prison sentence,” says Gharaei. Lead producer Milad Khosravi at Tehran-based Seven Springs Pictures , who joins Gharaei on the call as an interpreter, adds for context that the director has been the target of a “huge” disinformation campaign by government-controlled official media. “They are aggressively threatening him, and he has received thousands of hostile messages on social media. Given the scale and intensity of the threats, it would be dangerous for him to return to the country.” Khosravi is joined as co-lead producer by Odessa Rae of RaeFilm Studios ( The Voice of Hind Rajab) , who brought Max Richter onto the film, with music by Richter. News in July of the Venice selection for Falling House sparked outrage on Iranian regime-controlled news sites following the posting of images from the film showing Marzban not wearing a hijab, in a direct challenge to Islamic Republic rules requiring women to cover their hair. Gharaei notes that while he has never liked making women wear the hijab on his sets, it was not the main issue for him as he navigated government restrictions and censorship to get the production off the ground. Rather, it was the film’s searing critique of Iranian patriarchal society under the Islamic Republic regime. “More than the hijab, the biggest issue was the concept of the film and the core of the story… the regime would never have allowed us to make the film… that was the biggest challenge,” he says. Given the size of the production, Gharaei says it would have been impossible to shoot the film clandestinely, so he had to go down the route of securing a state production permit. “We had to find a way of working with the authorities,” he says. “In the end, we gave them a kind of fake script to get the written permission that allowed us to shoot the film, to have all the cast and crew on the set, and to make the film we wanted to make.” Mindful of the fact that Iran’s Production Permit Council can send in inspectors, or even place informers on set, Gharaei shot sensitive scenes with a reduced crew. “For scenes without a hijab or with sensitive dialogue, I allowed only a handful of people on set,” he says. “The risk of anything leaking to the government was simply too great.” “For the scenes without the hijab, it was sometimes just me with Laleh and the cameraman, or sometimes we pretended we were rehearsing or practicing, which was also safer.” Some regime detractors have suggested that the film’s setting of a house on the verge of being reduced to rubble is an insensitive reference to the U.S.-Iran war and even an insult to the memory of the country’s late supreme leader Ali Khomeini, who was killed on February 28 in a U.S.-Israeli airstrike on his official residence in Tehran. Gharaei dismisses the claims, pointing to the fact that he wrote the first draft of the screenplay in 2018, with the shoot beginning in November 2025 and wrapping in January 2026, just as widespread pro-democracy protests kicked off. He notes, however, that the film does foretell the war. “I’ve always thought that, given the way my country and the government are dealing with others, its neighbors and everything, war was unavoidable… the film is indirectly showing that,” says Gharaei. The Islamic Republic regime would go on to quash the pro-democracy protests in a brutal crackdown, which is believed to have left some 30,000 people dead. A second wave of protests began in mid-February but came to a halt with the U.S. and Israeli military campaign. With all eyes around the world on Iran’s next steps, amid questions over whether the regime will fall or survive, Gharaei says the ultimate interpretation of the film lies with the spectator. “The film is not saying that a war is needed. I didn’t seek to answer whether the war is a solution or not. I just show exterior forces sitting there, ready to attack and take advantage of this home at the same time as the pressure of the dictatorship and patriarchal system bears down… With all my films, my main goal and first responsibility as a director, is to tell a story and to tell it well. The social and political layers come after, with people bringing their own understanding to it.” ‘Tomb Raider’ Series Broke UK Safety Laws During Production Busan Unveils Lineup & Guests Yeoh, Huppert, Gyllenhaal, Rintaro Trump Backs Federal Film/TV Tax Credit, Calls Hollywood “A Total Disaster!” All Eyez On Guilty: Jury Reaches Verdict In Tupac Shakur’s 1996 Shooting Death Read More About: Comments

title: Cynthia Erivo, Andrew Scott, Ava DuVernay, Jesse Eisenberg & More Set For London Film Festival Screen Talks Program
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana Tom Hiddleston Thriller ‘Tenzing’ To Open Zurich Film Festival Marketing Executive Kevin Harrington Launches New Entertainment Agency Patrick Patrick International Disruptors: Megan Park Talks Debut Series ‘Sterling Point’, Importance Of “Not Talking Down” To Young Audiences & Stepping Out Of YA Space With Next Feature ‘Die Alive’ View All September 1, 2026 3:14am Andrew Scott, Ava DuVernay, Brad Bird, Cynthia Erivo, James Gray, Jesse Eisenberg, John Malkovich, Mahershala Ali, Naomi Ackie, Sofia Coppola & Danny Boyle London Film Festival The BFI London Film Festival has unveiled its list of filmmakers and actors participating in this year’s program of Screen Talks . The line-up includes Andrew Scott ( All of Us Strangers ); Ava DuVernay ( Selma ); Brad Bird ( The Incredibles ); Cynthia Erivo ( Wicked ); James Gray ( We Own the Night ); Jesse Eisenberg ( A Real Pain ); John Malkovich ( In the Line of Fire ); Mahershala Ali ( Moonlight ); Naomi Ackie ( Blink Twice ); Sofia Coppola ( The Virgin Suicides ); and Danny Boyle ( Slumdog Millionaire ). Scott will join to talk about a career that includes a BAFTA-winning performance as the nemesis of Sherlock Holmes , his role in Hamlet and a bold reinvention of Uncle Vanya as well as his performance of Ian Charleson in the LFF Opening Night film Elsinore . Watch on Deadline Related Stories Festivals Jesse Eisenberg's 'The Debut' With Julianne Moore & Paul Giamatti To Close BFI London Film Festival News Filmmaker Snigdha Kapoor Talks Dismantling Gender Norms In Coming-Of-Age Queer Identity Short Film 'Holy Curse': "We Are Losing Our Tolerance For Accepting People Who Have Different Values From Ours" DuVernay will talk about her work such as A Wrinkle in Time , dramas Selma and Origin and Oscar-nominated documentary 13 th while Bird will explore his Oscar and BAFTA-winning career in animated features including The Iron Giant , The Incredibles and Ratatouille as well as live-action titles Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol and Tomorrowland . Erivo will talk about her powerful performances on stage and screen. She rose to international prominence with her Tony Award-winning performance in The Color Purple on Broadway and has since starred in films including Harriet, Bad Times at the El Royale, Wicked, and Wicked: For Good . Gray, who is coming off the back of Paper Tiger which premiered in Cannes, will discuss his critically acclaimed career from his feature debut, Little Odessa to projects such as The Yards, We Own the Night, Two Lovers, The Immigrant and Armageddon Time – films that span a variety of genres but are all grounded in a gritty, earthy reality. He’ll also talk about The Lost City of Z and Ad Astra , which unfolded in very different worlds. Eisenberg will talk about his work in front of and behind the camera as he unveils the Festival’s Gala Closing Night Film, The Debut . A Broadway stage actor since he was 12, Eisenberg first moved into television with the series Get Real in 1999, before winning plaudits for his performances in the films Roger Dodger and The Squid and the Whale . Adventureland and Zombieland brought his wider recognition, followed by his portrayal of Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network . Alongside frequent screen appearances and contributions to The New Yorker, Eisenberg branched into filmmaking with When You Finish Saving the World and award-winning title A Real Pain . Acclaimed screen and theatre actor Malkovich will also touch down at LFF to discuss how he has spent his career forging indelible, charismatic, singular characters. He ranks as one of the only actors to feature in a film in which his own persona has a starring role, in Being John Malkovich. Oscar and BAFTA winner Ali worked in film and television for almost two decades before his pivotal and award-winning breakthrough performance in Moonlight . Since then, he has had roles in House of Cards and Free State of Jones to Green Book, True Detective and Leave the World Behind . Ackie’s credits include The End of the F***ing World , Education , the fifth part of Steve McQueen’s Small Axe series, Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker, Blink Twice, Mickey 17 and Sorry Baby , for which she received an Independent Spirit Award. Filmmakers Coppola and Boyle will also touch down at the festival where each will discuss their respective careers behind the camera. Coppola’s feature debut was The Virgin Suicides and her sophomore feature Lost in Translation saw her earn a Best Original Screenplay Academy Award. A perceptive study on celebrity, it’s a theme she continued to mine in Somewhere, The Bling Ring, On the Rocks and Priscilla. Boyle, meanwhile, hit cinema screens with his debut Shallow Grave before the era-defining Trainspotting. The Beach, 28 Days Later and Sunshine highlighted his gift for moving seamlessly between genres, before the enormous awards success of Slumdog Millionaire . He directed the Opening Ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics to huge acclaim, before returning to cinema with Steve Jobs, Yesterday and 28 Years Later . Boyle will discuss his wide-ranging career at HOME Manchester, the festival’s first Screen Talk outside of London. Also joining for a discussion — in which the creative reflects on their processes, influences and careers in depth in front of an audience at BFI Southbank in central London — are Oscar-nominated actor John Malkovich ( Being John Malkovich , Dangerous Liaisons ), U.S. filmmakers Sofia Coppola ( Lost in Translation , Marie Antoinette ), Ava DuVernay ( Selma , 13th ), Brad Bird ( The Incredibles , Ratatouille ) and James Gray ( Ad Astra , Paper Tiger ). The film follows a shy woman who is unexpectedly cast in a local production of an original musical. Under the spell of the strong-willed and enigmatic director, she loses herself in the role and the high-stakes world of this community theatre production. title: Diane Von Furstenberg to Honor Jane Fonda in Venice; Tina Brown and Karlie Kloss to Present

Set to take place in Venice, Italy on Sept. 3, a date that coincides with this year’s Venice Film Festival , Furstenberg will fete Jane Fonda , Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Amor Mottley, Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist Lynsey Addario, Food4Education founder and CEO Wawira Njiru and author, advocate and survivor Gisèle Pelicot. Held at Teatro Carlo Goldoni, the ceremony will also feature media maven Tina Brown and Karlie Kloss as presenters with a performance by singers Noa and Mira Awad. Related Stories Movies Andrew Scott, Cynthia Erivo, Jesse Eisenberg Among Star-Studded London Film Festival Screen Talk Slate News Ari Emanuel and His Brothers Donate $550,000 to Palestinian Doctor Training Program “For the 17th year of the DVF Awards, I am excited to honor women who have the courage to fight, the strength to survive and the leadership to inspire,” said von Furstenberg in a statement. Von Furstenberg and the Diller-von Furstenberg Family Foundation launched the DVF Awards in 2010 as a way to spotlight and support “extraordinary women” dedicated to “transforming the lives of other women; women who have had the courage to fight, the strength to survive and the leadership to inspire.” Five trophies are handed out to women along with a grant to each honoree, a gift bestowed to their respective nonprofit organizations to help propel and support their work. This year’s lineup covers such causes as environmental protection, political leadership, frontline journalism, food and education and advocacy for survivors. The DVF Awards also come at a time of immense challenges globally across the political and social landscape. More about the event and Furstenberg’s empire can be found here . title: In ‘Until the Day Ends,’ Two Serbs on Opposite Sides of a Deeply Divided Society Fall for Each Other (Exclusive Venice Trailer)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All September 1, 2026 1:45am 'Until the Day Ends' Courtesy of Venice Film Festival With her debut feature, the Serbian protest drama Until the Day Ends ( Do Kraja Dana ), Jelena Maksimović becomes the first female director from Serbia to bring a narrative feature to the official selection at the Venice Film Festival since Soja Jovanović’s Eagles Fly Early in 1966. That is likely to make for an emotional journey for the filmmaker to the festival, which just seems fitting. After all, an emotional, and intense, journey is also what the protagonists of her movie embark on. The film, set against anti-government protests by students and others in the country’s capital, Belgrade, will world premiere in the Horizons (Orrizonti) section of the 83rd edition of the Italian festival on Sept. 10. Serbia has experienced its largest wave of student protests and civil unrest in decades since the collapse of a railway station canopy killed 16 people in November 2024. Related Stories Movies 'Club Kid,' 'Bunker' and Danny Boyle's 'Ink' Added to Zurich Film Festival Lineup Movies In 'Love Is the Monster,' Paulina García Is a Granny Facing Impossible Choices (Exclusive TIFF Trailer) Until the Day Ends stars Lena Trifunović as Lena, an anarchist student, and Andrija Krivokapić as Stefan, a working-class youth with friends who are pro-government loyalists. Forget Romeo and Juliet! Set against the backdrop of the student protests in and around Belgrade, the two may be on opposite sides of a deeply divided society, but fall for each other. When a stone is thrown and hits a policeman, Stefan fears he is to blame, leading the duo to flee the city together, adding a road movie vibe to the film. Irina Hotomski, Stefan Tarabić and Miodrag Dragičević are also part of the cast. The director co-wrote Until the Day Ends with Olga Dimitrijevic and Ivan Salatic. Paul Spengemann ( Der Fleck ) is the cinematographer, and Jan Klemsche ( God Will Not Help ) the editor. Heretic is handling sales on the film. If the film sounds like one for you to explore, THR can now exclusively premiere a clip from it ahead of its Venice debut. Caution: things get tense here! But you were likely already expecting that. title: ‘Love Island USA’ Season 8 Reunion Sees Fiery Islander Confrontations, Tear-Filled Moments and More
full_text: Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 12:25am 'Love Island USA' season eight reunion. Christine Bartolucci/Peacock Logo text Nothing was off limits at Peacock ‘s Love Island USA season eight reunion that saw the winners, fan-favorite Islanders and bombshells reunite to unpack some of the season’s biggest and most drama-filled moments. Ariana Madix and Andy Cohen co-hosted the reunion special that aired Monday night and was filmed in front of a live studio audience in Los Angeles. The reunion featured winners Trinity and Bryce , as well as finalists Aniya and Carl, Kayda and Zach, and Melanie and Sincere. However, the other OG Islanders and bombshells from the latest season were also in attendance to help stir the night’s drama. Related Stories TV 'Love Island USA' Returns for Season 8 Reunion: When and Where to Watch Online TV 'Love Island USA' Renewed for Season 9, Peacock Drops Season 8 Reunion Teaser After showing never-before-seen videos of the finalists when they first got their phones back and saw America’s reaction in July following the season eight finale, Madix and Cohen didn’t waste any time diving right in. The night also featured a classic Kenzie split, Trinity and Bryce talking about life outside the villa, Islanders’ reactions to fan comments, the couples revealing who’s still together post- Love Island USA and more. Below, The Hollywood Reporter unpacks the season’s eighth reunion’s most memorable moments. And if you want to relive all the season’s jaw-dropping moments , check out THR ‘s coverage and interviews here . Aniya, Tierra and KC Squash Any Beef Following one of the season’s most dramatic moments, when KC left Aniya single after he chose to couple up with Casa Amor bombshell Titi, leading to a fiery confrontation between the Islanders, a surprising friendship later developed on the show between Titi and Aniya. However, comments Titi and KC made on their Aftersun episode after being dumped from the villa left Aniya confused about where their dynamic stood. “I feel like at the moment I had no beef with Titi at all,” Aniya said. “It was more the situation with KC and what happened. Honestly, I was kind of like taken aback a little bit when you’re on Aftersun , you were like, ‘Oh, I’m not going to be friends with anyone outside of this, really.’ Why did you say that?” Titi then took a moment to clarify her past comment. “I didn’t say I want to be friends with anyone . I said I didn’t want to be friends with everyone , and that wasn’t regarding you,” she said before asking, “Is there a reason why you felt that was directed towards you?” “I was kind of really thrown off with the whole Aftersun [episode], especially with both of you guys,” Aniya replied. “I feel like we’ve been on good terms, and then KC proceeded to say, ‘Oh, Aniya’s fragile,’ and I feel like you just contradicted the whole apology that we had in there. I haven’t spoken badly on you guys at all, so it really hurt my feelings a little bit.” KC also took the opportunity to apologize to Aniya over his “fragile” remark. “I could have said a different word,” he said. “I would hate for you to think I have anything against you, you know what I mean? I think we’re all left on good terms and that’s where I want to be.” Madix and Cohen on Love Island USA season eight reunion. Christine Bartolucci/Peacock Kenzie and Melanie Squabble Over Airtime Comment and “Non-Existent” Friendship Madix asked Kenzie to clarify her alleged comment on Sol’s Instagram live last month about Melanie having more airtime than everyone else. “After watching the show back, I did see that she did get a lot more airtime, but I would never talk shit about her,” Kenzie said. After Kenzie called out Melanie for rolling her eyes, she added, “This isn’t about you. It’s just the show and you did get more [air]time because you guys had more stuff going on in y’all’s relationship.” In response, Melanie said, “It just caught me off guard that everyone’s together and that it’s even a conversation. I have not done anything to you.” She also accused Kenzie of never being there for her throughout their time in the villa, despite Kenzie calling Melanie her best friend. “These girls [Trinity, Aniya and Kayda] were there for me,” Melanie said before sharing an example of Kenzie’s betrayal of their friendship. “There was a moment when me and Corbin got put together. You completely dipped on me. You did not talk to me. You didn’t even check up on me. I had to see my couple be with someone else. You did not care about me. I never had a chat with you. I didn’t pull you. You didn’t pull me.” After Madix pointed out that “it seems like this friendship is essentially non-existent” at the moment, the host asked if there’s a path forward for them. After Kenzie expressed through tears that she still loves Melanie, the latter also shared that “everything is fixable,” including their friendship. Sol and Melanie Get in Fiery Exchange: “Mama a Liar” After Cohen reminded the audience that Sol previously said on social media she wanted her fellow Islanders to “feel your wrath tonight,” he gave her an opportunity to share what’s on her mind. Sol was ultimately dumped from the villa earlier in the season after Sincere recoupled with Melanie. “Where do we start? When I first came in, I feel like you guys were welcoming the first day, and then I started talking to Sincere, and then the energy just got fucking weird in the house. And I was like, whoa, I don’t know what’s going on,” Sol said. “Also, me watching it back, I’m like, damn, y’all were objectifying my body and like just saying like a bunch of different stuff.” Melanie quickly chimed in, saying, “I am actually shocked about you.” “I am actually shocked because as soon as America put you and Sincere together, I’ve never once came at you crazy ever,” she continued. “In fact, I actually pulled you aside in Say Less, and I got to know you. I sat with you. We spoke about your dad. We spoke about your friendships. … I was so genuine.” Melanie also called out Sol for claiming on social media post-villa that she was pied more than twice during one of the challenges. “You didn’t. You’re a liar. Mama a liar,” Melanie stated. Despite Sol doubling down that she was pied more, Cohen later confirmed that she was in fact only pied by two boys during said challenge. Following a heated exchange between the two women, Melanie shouted, “You’re lying. You’re trying to build this victim’s story, but it’s not.” She also noted that “we tried” to befriend Sol in the villa. However, Sol angrily replied, “It’s not about you. It’s about me and my experience. She also maintained her stance that she felt the girls never genuinely wanted to be her friend. Love Island USA season eight reunion. Christine Bartolucci/Peacock Trinity Confronts Sol Over Her Remarks About Relationship With Bryce Despite Trinity and Bryce becoming the ultimate winners of Love Island USA season eight, Sol previously questioned their relationship while answering fan questions during an Instagram live. In response, Trinity took a moment during the reunion to confront Sol. “I didn’t like the way that you went on live and started talking about me and Bryce,” Trinity said. She was specifically frustrated with Sol claiming Bryce pulled Kayda for a chat four or five times in the villa, despite being coupled up with Trinity. However, he actually only asked to talk to Kayda once. “Y’all keep bringing up this one time where he pulled Kayda,” Trinity said. “There’s been times I wanted to talk to Corbin; I wanted to talk to Sean. Nobody bring that shit up.” Bryce also chimed in, adding, “Everyone’s saying it’s Couples Island and everyone’s closed off. But when I pull one person for a chat, and now, I don’t love my person.” After hearing Trinity and Bryce out, Sol apologized for her past comments. “I will say I worded that completely wrong,” she said. “I 100 percent apologize for that.” Which Couples Are Still Together Post-Show? In addition to all the season eight finalists still being together and continuing to grow their connections, Titi and KC, and Dylan and Kenzie are also still in relationships post-show. However, Parmida and Corbin’s romantic spark has since ended. As for why they’re no longer in a relationship, Corbin said, “Our chemistry together was fantastic. Our energy was 100 percent with each other. We’re compatible in some ways. It’s just coming out into the real world, we had some ups and downs. But as two people come together [and] come to an understanding, you know, two people just don’t work out.” Parmida added, “I just feel like a relationship right now is not what we need. Better as friends.” THR

title: ‘The Varnell Hill Show’ Review: Tommy Davidson in Paramount+’s Amiable Throwback of a ‘Martin’ Spinoff
full_text: × Skip to main content By Angie Han Plus Icon Angie Han Television Critic ajhan Follow Sign Up View All September 1, 2026 12:00am Tommy Davidson as Varnell Hill in 'The Varnell Hill Show.' Paramount+ “I got just one question for you: Did you miss me?” So goes the catchphrase for Varnell Hill ( Tommy Davidson ), the late-night talk show host who first graced our screens in Martin some 30-odd years ago. I’ll leave you to determine how much you personally have been longing to revisit a character who, for all his vivid personality, only ever appeared in two episodes of that earlier series. But hearing that line again in his new spinoff, Paramount+’s The Varnell Hill Show , it feels easy enough to answer in the affirmative. If the workplace comedy works better as a reminder of times gone by than a breath of fresh air, it nonetheless makes for a pleasantly nostalgic time. Related Stories TV 'Martin' Spinoff 'The Varnell Hill Show' Sets Premiere Date Movies Dave Chappelle Pitches Eddie Murphy on Joining Potential 'Chappelle's Show' Reboot at AFI Gala The Varnell Hill Show The Bottom Line More nostalgic than fresh, for better or worse. Airdate: Tuesday, Sept. 1 (Paramount+) Cast: Tommy Davidson, Wendy Raquel Robinson, Chris Williams, Nick Cafero, Emmanuel Hudson, Kym Whitley Creators: Kevin G. Boyd, Sherri McGee McCovey, Bentley Kyle Evans Despite its connection to Martin , no real knowledge of the earlier show is required to watch this one. Aside from a few passing references (“My cousin from Detroit told me to tell you, “Wazzup?”), creators Kevin G. Boyd, Sherri McGee McCovey and Bentley Kyle Evans rarely bring up past events or characters; even Martin star and creator (and Varnell Hill executive producer) Martin Lawrence guest stars only as a completely different character. As for Varnell, not much seems to be different for the self-described “one-time radio king, two-time ex-husband — soon to be three — and eight-time Soul Train Awards presenter.” He’s still an outgoing, egotistical personality, and still played by Davidson with loads of charisma and a knack for big but precise physical comedy. He’s still hosting the same old talk show to the same old, now rapidly aging audience. His most loyal aides, yes-man/bestie Tre (Chris Williams) and assistant Kym (Kym Whitley), are ones who’ve been with him for ages. But change is coming for Varnell, whether he likes it or not. (He very much does not.) The network CEO who once championed him has been pushed out, replaced by the useless nepo baby son (Nick Cafero’s Jonah) who despises Varnell precisely because the old man adored him. Jonah’s plan to oust Varnell involves installing an ambitious new executive producer (Wendy Raquel Robinson’s Rachel) ostensibly to help boost ratings, but in actuality to annoy Varnell into quitting over creative differences. Despite the season primarily revolving around the efforts to freshen up the talk show for a wider (i.e., younger) demographic, not much about The Varnell Hill Show reads as particularly modern, for better or for worse. Its format — multi-cam, laugh-tracked, with the occasional fourth-wall-breaking aside — is one that would have been in vogue when Martin originally aired. It’s done quite well (and of the supporting cast, Robinson and Whitley, both veterans of sitcoms from that era, seem so at home that you’d think they’d been on this brand-new show for years already), but whether that makes it feel hoary or comforting will probably depend on whether you grew up watching similar series. Its storylines tend to stick to well-trod territory: Varnell not understanding social media, Varnell trying to seem younger, Varnell accidentally getting high on pot brownies. Even a multi-episode arc featuring a Gen Z comic who seems primed to supplant Varnell as the network’s new darling betrays little understanding of who Marshay (Brittney Ayona Clemons) is beyond “younger than Varnell.” Its jokes are occasionally stale — sometimes in ways that seem appropriate for the characters (of course Varnell is the sort of guy who’d drop a Kato Kaelin reference three decades after the O.J. trial) and sometimes in ways that suggest The Varnell Hill Show itself might benefit from some fresher blood behind the scenes (it makes no sense that a Millennial hypebeast-type writer would describe Moo Deng as a top comedy trend in 2026). The inconsistency can make it difficult to tell exactly what the vibe of Varnell’s program is meant to be. In one episode, Varnell goes viral for an accidentally live-streamed rant complaining of being treated by top brass like “a TikTok Bojangles” and declaring that, “When I speak my truth, it’s aggressive” — a slightly confusing statement given that what we’ve seen of his public persona up to that point is so easygoing that earlier that day, he’d been boasting of how many grandmas fall asleep to him. (“And a lot of them don’t wake up,” Jonah snarks in response.) Still, there’s an earnestness to the series that makes it easy to vibe with. The challenges faced by a Black host and his mostly Black staff in trying to create something that feels good and authentic at a company run by white men, at least one of whom is hell-bent on ruining them, is an intermittently important theme throughout the eight-part season. And there’s an element of wish fulfillment in seeing Varnell and Rachel and their colleagues triumph by, for example, giving a MAGA-era Kanye West stand-in the takedown he deserves (even if, again, the real-life reference feels a few years old). Then there’s the endless rotation of celebrities playing themselves. Varnell’s show might be fictional, but the show about his show actually does function as a way to spotlight Black talents across the industry. Doug E. Fresh is the program’s bandleader, while the likes of Damon Wayans and Matt Barnes come through as talk show guests and Kirk Franklin and Omarion as musical guests. In one of the comic highlights of the season, Deon Cole, Mike Epps, Lavell Crawford and Miss Pat play themselves as friends of Varnell’s who’ve been invited to roast him for an anniversary special; the chemistry that flows from the segment really does have the joyous, unfiltered feel of old friends just trying to crack each other up. Ironically, or perhaps appropriately, the most glaring issue with the series, aside from its old-timey-ness, likely would have been less of one in the 1990s: the fact that there simply doesn’t seem to be enough of it. Like so many first seasons, The Varnell Hill Show ’s has the feel of a newcomer trying out everything it can to see what sticks. But at just eight half-hour episodes, it simply doesn’t have time to figure out what to do with supporting ensemble members like AJ (Emmanuel Hudson), Varnell’s dopey social media manager of a nephew, or flesh out ones like hopelessly square head writer Thad (Neil Brown Jr.) and his staff. If Paramount+ is putting its weight behind this amiable throwback of a series, it might as well go all the way and give it another dozen or 20 episodes to find its most fully realized self. THR

title: Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger…
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic All Eyez On Guilty: Tupac Trial Jury Reaches Verdict In ‘Poetic Justice’ Star’s 1996 Drive-By Shooting Death Trump Backs Federal Film & TV Tax Incentive: “Hollywood Is A Complete & Total Disaster!” Chief Justice Calls Trump Ballroom “Unlawful”; POTUS Brags Of Supreme Court Approval On Final Construction Of $600M Venue View All August 24, 2026 1:11am Story Arc California Attorney General Rob Bonta Getty There will be no settlement talks meeting Monday between Paramount and a coalition of state attorneys general after all. “My office was scheduled to meet with Paramount on Monday, August 24th,” California AG Rob Bonta said late late Sunday. “I have pulled down this meeting.” Related Stories News The ParaBros Backlash: Threats To Leave L.A. & An AG Who Won’t Back Down Divide Hollywood Legal Paramount Denies Leaking Details Of Talks With CA AG’s Office, Company “Hopeful” And “Ready To Continue Good Faith Discussions” Bonta canceled the scheduled sit-down after reports of an August 21 meeting with the David Ellison -led company oozed out. More galling to Bonta is that what was discussed at that meeting slipped out into the public sphere. The re-election seeking AG specifically noted: “My office had a meeting with Paramount on Friday. Paramount did not maintain the confidentiality of that meeting.” “Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” the AG said in a statement provided to Deadline in the midnight hour. “As soon as Paramount stops playing games and engages sincerely, my office is happy to meet again.” Watch on Deadline News of behind-the-scenes talks in the bitter battle over Paramount’s $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery were actually first confirmed publicly by none other than Gov. Gavin Newsom . “I know there are many meetings that are going on, and there’s a lot of conversation,” the presumed 2028 presidential candidate said on August 21. It should be noted that Deadline actually heard details of the August 21 preliminary gathering to set the agenda for the August 24 meeting from a variety of sources, if you know what I mean? Though expectations for the August 24 meeting were “intentionally low,” sources told Deadline Sunday, there seemed to be several hot ticket items on the table for the parties. Specifically, representatives of the 12 state AGs who sued Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery in an antitrust action on July 13 wanted CEO Ellison to sell a swath of WBD’s still lucrative cable channel stable. As well, the elected officials sought to have Paramount and WB remain two separate studios, with Donald Trump pal Ellison (and to some extent his father and backer Larry Ellison) practically cordoned off from running the place he just bought. “David’s not going to go along with any of that, and Bonta knows it,” a studio exec told Deadline Sunday of the discussion points put on the table. Clear non-starters with Ellison and Para execs, the agenda points also reflect the wide figurative and literal distance between the AGs, their lawsuit partners the WGA and the Melrose lot. Paramount did not respond early Monday to request for comment on Bonta’s pulling of the meeting plug. The New York Times first reported the meeting cancellation. Urged by the likes of Gov. Newsom, flip-flopping L.A. Mayor Karen Bass, the DGA, IATSE , Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra, and others to sit down and hammer out a settlement, the AGs and Paramount/WBD have been set by a federal judge to go to trial on March 2, 2027. David Ellison, Chairman & CEO, Paramount Skydance Getty With Bonta decrying leaks of Ellison moving Paramount Skydance to Georgia, Texas or Tennessee if the ParaBros merger doesn’t see significant talks or resolution by October 1 as “blackmail,” the bitterness between the two has become as much a corporate and political showdown as a legal one. The CEO penning NYT op-eds i nsisting it is all about CNN, didn’t help the healing process. The already reinforced battlefronts became all the more stark over the past week, with Paramount ignoring federal Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin’s earlier implied rejection of any bond from the states and asking for a $1.88 billion bond to offset the “extraordinary losses” the suit could cost the company. Add to that another report submitted to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors on August 19 spotlighting that “about 4,500 TV and film jobs … could be lost.” The L.A. County Department of Economic Opportunity also estimates thousands of more indirect and industry adjacent jobs will be wiped out by the more than $80 billion debt-carrying ParaBros. The bigger picture puts another consequence of the merger being the loss of wages in the billions and the region losing $547 million in tax revenue. No further settlement meetings had been put on the calendar beyond today. One source said to Deadline the fight between Paramount and Bonta is all a “game of PR chicken.” If so, then someone just blinked. Late on Sunday, Bonta abruptly canceled the meeting. “They wanted to have the settlement discussions, and we are happy to hear them out,” Bonta said. “We thought that they were reaching out to us in good faith and sincerely, and the unfortunately, they violated the rules of engagement, and that was not okay. They leaked lies to the press while we were in settlement negotiations, and that’s not okay. That’s not acceptable. That is amateur hour. That is playing games.” Watch on Deadline Paramount issued a statement on Monday in which it said that it “has not been the source of the leaks of any of our confidential discussions with the AG’s office.” On Sunday, The Wall Street Journal reported, and confirmed by Deadline, that the AG’s asks included keeping the studios separate as well as unloading some cable networks. But there were earlier conversations between the parties. California Governor Gavin Newsom had indicated on Friday that there “are many meetings that are going on, and there’s a lot of conversation.” Bonta said, “It is the alleged disclosure of the substance of the conversations of what occurred in those meetings that is the problem. Those are required under federal law to be confidential, and for good reason. So you can be candid. So you can be productive. So maybe you can even be creative in those discussions. If you’re having confidential settlement discussions, and as you’re having them, one of the parties is going out to the press and representing to the press what’s being said by you in those negotiations and lying about it, whether it’s true or whether they’re lying, neither is acceptable.” A spokesperson for the attorney general later said that Paramount asked them to keep the contents of settlement negotiations confidential under Federal Evidence Code 408 but they believe “they turned around and disclosed it themselves.” The spokesperson said that they are not alleging that Paramount violated federal law at this time. title: Paramount-WBD Antitrust Suit Heads To Supreme Court In Red State Vs. Blue State Showdown Over $111B…
full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic ‘Obsession’ EP Sues Over Allegedly Being Scammed Out Of Promised Profits From High-Grossing Horror Hit All Eyez On Guilty: Tupac Trial Jury Reaches Verdict In ‘Poetic Justice’ Star’s 1996 Drive-By Shooting Death Trump Backs Federal Film & TV Tax Incentive: “Hollywood Is A Complete & Total Disaster!” View All August 26, 2026 8:03am Story Arc Getty Images UPDATED 8:03 AM: Iowa and Montana are going to the Supreme Court to put a halt on antitrust efforts to prevent the $111 billion merger between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery. This case is about the legal limits on politicized antitrust enforcement by a small handful of states seeking to enjoin a $110 billion merger that the United States, most American states, and competition regulators worldwide have cleared,” insists the two red states in their Motion for Leave to File a Bill of Complaint against the 12 blue state led by Golden State AG and MAGA anti-poster boy Rob Bonta . Related Stories Legal Paramount Denies Leaking Details Of Talks With CA AG’s Office, Company “Hopeful” And “Ready To Continue Good Faith Discussions” News Rob Bonta Says No Paramount-WBD Settlement Talks Scheduled After He Canceled Monday Session After threats Tuesday in an op-ed by Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird, the Hawkeye State and the Treasure State filed paperwork with the High Court late last night – and they want a fast response. Watch on Deadline “Expedited consideration now will alleviate the need for exceedingly hasty action later,” they state of the proposed stoppage of a ParaBros combo pending the initial litigation of July 13. “Mergers do not freeze well.” In fact, barely letting the situation sit on ice at all, Iowa and Montana are looking at a deadline of September 15 to be exact. That is two weeks before the $7 million a day ticking fee paid to WBD shareholders kicks in for the David Ellison -run Para. “It is no great burden to ask Defendant States to file their response on an accelerated timeline,” today’s filing asserts, citing Supreme Court Rule 21. “The case is not an emergency yet, but the deadline for the merger is June 2027, and there would be little hope of resolving the case by then if a decision on hearing it were made in January,” the filing adds. “That is especially so if the Court first addresses the threshold question of whether it even has discretion to deny audience on the merits for cases within its original and exclusive jurisdiction.” Awaiting a reaction from the conservative majority SCOTUS , which could reject or slow walk the request, Iowa and Montana’s action against the “State of Arizona, State of California, State of Colorado, State of Connecticut, Commonwealth of Massachusetts, State of Minnesota, State of Nevada, State of New Jersey, State of New Mexico, State of New York, State of Oregon, and State of Washington” is a roll of the dice for all concerned. If Iowa and Montana get their wish list and an early October hearing takes place (big ifs) it is very unlikely there would be any ruling from SCOTUS before late spring or early summer. A timeline that wouldn’t really be very helpful a Paramount that is looking at a June 4, 2027 expiration date on the merger if they don’t close. Also, SCOTUS sign-offs on such requests are not rare for the Roberts court, but they aren’t common either. Still, perhaps playing to their real audience, the Iowa and Montana motion also jumps into defending the Ellisons’ bottom line – as Bird did in her August 25 Daily Wire op-ed. Blasting the blue states for running counter to a merger approved by 67 jurisdictions worldwide and seemingly fast-tracked by Donald Trump ‘s DOJ,, the motion notes: “The costs are not limited to the companies themselves. Defendant States’ suit has injected uncertainty into every company that does business with Paramount or Warner Bros. Suppliers and other counterparties cannot make investment choices without knowing who the real decision maker is and whether the business relationship has a future once the deal closes (or does not close).” There has been no full-on response yet from Bonta, but don’t expect the media savvy CA AG to be silent too long on this latest challenge. “We are reviewing the filing and will respond as appropriate,” a spokesperson for Bonta told Deadline this AM. PREVIOUSLY, 10:09 PM: With friends like Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird, does Paramount and David Ellison really need enemies? In an op-ed penned for the conservative Daily Wire Tuesday, the Hawkeye State ally of Donald Trump is threatening to take California to the Supreme Court. Declaring that “California is once again trying to be the country’s regulator,” Bird wants to stop the antitrust lawsuit from the Golden State, New York and 10 other states against Paramount’s $111 billion purchase of Warner Brothers Discovery. “Just like California should keep its hands off America’s bacon, California needs to understand that it doesn’t get to decide what Americans can choose to watch or stream,” the reelection-seeking Bird states of the state and its AG Rob Bonta. “If California believes a transaction that 68 regulators approved is nevertheless illegal, it is free to make that argument,” she notes, lamenting the $7 million a day ticking fee and more Paramount will have to start paying WBD shareholders starting October 1. “But it should make it in the one court with the authority to bind all of us, and it should make it now, before the bill for the delay comes due,” Bird claps, leaving out any reference to the Empire State’s Letitia James and other AGs. Yet, for all her rallying to the ParaBros cause, as well as some variations on what Bonta and gang are actually alleging in the March 2, 2027 trial-starting case before a federal judge in Oakland, Bird doesn’t seem to have actually filed anything with SCOTUS. It also seems hard to see how even if Iowa did take California to the conservative majority Supreme Court, how they could get a hearing before next spring or even October, with the John Roberts-led high court not back in session until October 5. However, let’s sidestep Bird getting a perch on SCOTUS’ fast tracked interim relief docket (AKA the emergency docket or shadow docket) for a second, and look at a possible route under the provisions of Article III, Section 2 of the Constitution. Even if the case fell within the “original jurisdiction” criteria and passed muster with the Justices, any ruling would likely still be drawn out — likely beyond the March 2027 trial already on the calendar. In the rare case SCOTUS picks up such a state-to-state battle, it would generally appoint a “special master’ to review the matter before getting directly on it. All of which, like Paramount CEO Ellison accused Bonta in an August 4 NYT op-ed , makes Bird’s flag planter reek of politics. Bird, who filed a brief in 2024 in support of the former Apprentice host’s ultimately successful bid to gain significant immunity from prosecution for acts taken while POTUS, sidesteps most of the meat of the actual antitrust suit the 12 states and the WGA are pursuing. A suit that Bonta, in an August 10 guest column for Deadline , paints as “a straight up antitrust enforcement case. One that is very cut and dry.” Instead, Bird, while giving the DOJ the benefit of the doubt, moves to blast Bonta and colleagues as “more hostile to this pro-competition merger than Europe and China.” The ‘To Save American Movies, I’m Taking California To The Supreme Court’ entitled piece in the Ben Shapiro-founded outlet insists a ParaBros combo is good for high streaming subscription paying Iowans, competition and the movie and TV businesses. “The merger could create a company to compete: an estimated $6 billion in savings to reinvest, and a public commitment to release at least 30 movies in theaters every year. More movies mean more entertainment — and more competition means lower prices,” Bird says.
